(p-1) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah Ghafir, also called Surat al-Mu'min and Surat al-Tawl.

Its purpose is to provide proof for the last point of the preceding surah, which divides people in the Hereafter into two categories, and to give each what it deserves in perfect justice. The One who does this possesses complete might and all-encompassing knowledge. He has made clear, in the fullest clarity and in the manner of wisdom, what displeases Him and what pleases Him. Whoever does not surrender his whole affair to Him and disputes His signs that point to the Resurrection or other matters, by his words or his deeds, will be disgraced by Him, punished, and destroyed. This is indicated by the naming of the surah as "Ghafir" (the Forgiver), for none can forgive whom He wills whatever He wills except one of complete might, and none knows all sins so as to be their Forgiver except one of perfect knowledge. (p-2) The same applies to all the attributes mentioned in the verse concerning reward and punishment. Likewise with al-Tawl (the Bountiful): none can bestow unrestricted bounty except one who is like that, for whoever is deficient in might is limited, since some obstacle prevents him from certain bounties, and that can only come from deficiency of knowledge. Likewise the indication of the naming of the surah as "al-Mu'min" (the Believer): its story points to this aim, especially the matter of the Resurrection, which is the greatest concern and the supreme pivot for knowing the One who is worshipped. (In the name of Allah) the Great King, who gives each of His servants what he deserves, so that no one can contradict Him in any of that or oppose Him. (al-Rahman) who encompassed them all with His mercy in this world through creation, provision, and clarification, with nothing hidden in it. (al-Rahim) who singles out with His mercy whom He wills of His servants, making him wise, and great in this earth and in the dominion of the heavens.

﴿Ha Mim﴾ That is, this is the wisdom of Muhammad (ﷺ), which al-Rahman al-Rahim, al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy), al-Majid (the Glorious) bestowed upon him, from among the attributes of perfection that He possesses.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 2:

When the conclusion of the preceding surah established the perfection of Allah through His truthfulness in His promise and His threat, by sending each group to the abode He had prepared for it, it became established that the Book which contains that is from Him, and that He is of complete might (ʿizzah), of perfect knowledge, and comprehensive of all attributes of perfection. So He said: ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾, meaning the comprehensive one, containing the limits (ḥudūd), the rulings (aḥkām), the knowledge (maʿārif), and the honouring (ikrām) of everything that is needed, by sending it down gradually according to what is beneficial and to bring it closer to the minds that are dull and limited, and to train the intellects that soar in the atmosphere of meanings. ﴿From Allah﴾, meaning the one who combines all the attributes of perfection. And since the consideration here, among all the attributes, is more directed towards might and knowledge, because the context is the establishment of truthfulness in promise and threat, He said: ﴿the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾.

Imam Abu Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr said: When Allah, glorified is He, opened the surah of az-Zumar (the Groups) with sincere devotion (ikhlāṣ), and mentioned its cause and what moves to it by the permission of Allah, which is the Book, and followed that with the compensation of mentioning those whose description the surah of Ṣād was built upon, and the verses continued on this purpose up to their rebuke by the parable which He struck, the clear example in His words: ﴿Allah strikes a parable: a man in whom are partners quarrelling, and a man belonging wholly to one man﴾ [az-Zumar: 29]. He described the partners as quarrelling (mushākasah), because by this purpose it becomes clear that none of them has a consistent aim. He also mentioned the ugliness of their excuse in their saying: ﴿We do not worship them except that they bring us nearer to Allah in closeness﴾ [az-Zumar: 3]. Then He, exalted is He, followed with informing of His subjugation and might, so that no one forsaken would imagine that any matter escapes His hand and His subjugation. So Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is Allah not sufficient for His servant?﴾ [az-Zumar: 36], up to His words: ﴿Is Allah not Mighty, Possessor of retribution?﴾ [az-Zumar: 37]. Then He followed that with the state of their rivals, that they neither harm nor benefit, so He said: ﴿Say: Have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah should intend me some harm, could they remove His harm? Or if He should intend me mercy, could they withhold His mercy?﴾ [az-Zumar: 38]. Then He followed this with what corresponds to it of the evidences of His might, so He said: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs all intercession﴾ [az-Zumar: 44]; ﴿Say: O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾ [az-Zumar: 46]; ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it?﴾ [az-Zumar: 52]; ﴿Allah is the Creator of all things﴾ [az-Zumar: 62]; ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾ [az-Zumar: 63]. Then He rebuked and reproached them for their ignorance, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is it other than Allah you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?﴾ [az-Zumar: 64]. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿They have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand﴾ [az-Zumar: 67]. Then He, exalted is He, followed that by mentioning the effects of might and subjugation, so He mentioned the blowing into the Horn for the swoon, then the blast of rising and recompense, and the destiny of the two groups. So blessed is the One alone in might and subjugation. When these verses included, among the effects of His might and subjugation, what has been pointed to in part, He followed that with His words, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾ [Ghafir: 1], ﴿The revelation of the Book from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾. So He mentioned from His names, glorified is He, these two great names, as an alert to His singularity in what they necessitate, and that He is the true Mighty, the subjugator of creation, because of His exalted knowledge of the aspects of wisdom that were hidden from creation: that He deferred the decisive recompense to the Hereafter, and made this world an abode of trial and testing, along with His subjugation of all in both abodes together, and their being not outside His dominion and subjugation. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance﴾ [Ghafir: 3], as a consolation for those who responded with His praise and turned in repentance by His kindness, and in keeping with the rule of mercy and its preponderance. Then He said: ﴿Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty﴾ [Ghafir: 3], so that the believer takes the necessary implications of servitude from fear and hope. He enclosed His words ﴿Severe in punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 3] between His words ﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance﴾ [Ghafir: 3] and His words ﴿Possessor of bounty﴾ [Ghafir: 3]. By His words, ﴿Let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾ [Ghafir: 4], glorified is He, He pointed back to His earlier words ﴿And He has caused us to inherit the earth﴾ [az-Zumar: 74], as though the sense is: if the final outcome belongs to you and your followers, then do not be concerned about their movement throughout the land. Then He, exalted is He, explained that their state in this is like the state of the nations before them, and their disputing in the signs is like their disputing, and that this is because the word of punishment has been justly decreed against them, and what was previously determined for them in the Mother of the Book. The end.

When the preceding verse (the end of that surah) stated that the word of punishment had come due against the disbelievers, this might have led someone who was entrenched in disbelief to despair of success, and made him think that departing from disbelief was impossible. Forgiveness, which is the erasure of sin both in its essence and in its traces, is consequent upon knowledge of the sin and the power to forgive, and the attributes that follow from these are the result of might. Here the verse points to both, while soliciting the compassion of every sinner and negligent person, with His words: ﴿Forgiver of sin﴾, meaning, with repentance or without repentance, as He wills. This attribute belongs to Him always, so it is definite. Al-Samin said: Sibawayh stated explicitly that every idafah (genitive construction) that is not pure (mahdah) may be made pure and the definite nouns may be described by it, except the sifah mushabbahah (the resembling attributive adjective). The Kufans did not make any exception.

Since the placing of forgiveness before repentance conveyed that forgiveness does not depend on repentance except in the case of shirk (polytheism), and since the polytheists used to say: "We have committed shirk, killed, and gone to extremes in sins, so our return will not be accepted, and there is no benefit for us in embracing Islam," He encouraged them to repent by mentioning it, and by joining it with the conjunction "and" [p-6], which indicates the firmness of the attribute, to inform them that no sin is too great for Him. So He said: ﴿and Acceptor of repentance﴾. He left the verbal noun (al-masdar) in its bare form so that it would be understood that the least of what is called by this name is sufficient. Making it a noun of genus, like its companions, is more appropriate than making it a plural among them, like tamr and tamrah.

Since limiting the discourse to encouragement, by what raised hope, might embolden the one persisting in transgression against His severity, He said, dropping the conjunction, so that the attribute would not be felt as a sign of the firmness that both the conjunction and the sifah mushabbahah imply. This is to inform them of His hidden gentleness, that His mercy precedes His wrath, and that if He were to display all the might He possesses, He would destroy everyone upon it, as is indicated by the form of mutual action (mufa'alah) in ﴿Were Allah to take people to task for their wrongdoing﴾ [al-Nahl: 61], since when an act is between two parties it is more intense. ﴿Severe in punishment﴾. Moreover, its indefiniteness and vagueness, as al-Zamakhshari said, serve to indicate extreme severity and that nothing is more calamitous or bitter than it, for the sake of increasing the warning, and this is more subtle than the indication of the conjunction had it been used.

When He had completed the encouragement through pardon and the warning through punishment, He followed it with the stimulation of desire for grace, and He said, dropping the conjunction because completeness does not require emphasis, and omission does not spoil the purpose, for the evidence of reason is established upon the perfection of His attributes: ﴿Possessor of bounty﴾, meaning, abundance of grace and favor, power, wealth, plenitude and benevolence, none resembles Him in any of that nor comes near Him. Then He gave as the reason for His firmness in all of that His oneness, and He said: ﴿There is no god but He﴾. When this whole matter produced His singularity, it certainly produced His words: ﴿To Him﴾, meaning, to Him alone, ﴿is the final return﴾, meaning, in meaning in this world, and in sensory and meaningful terms in the Hereafter, so that each of these attributes becomes fully manifest, such that no ambiguity remains in any of it. For it is not sound in wisdom that someone should oppress the servants and then die in might without retribution, so that the one oppressed is lost, because this is a matter that the least of people would not accept among his own servants.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 4:

When it became clear what comprehensive clarity the Qur'an possesses in accordance with its revelation, as a response to the doubts that are presented to them, it indicated, by removing every cause of doubt, the attributes of might and knowledge which He, glorified be He, ascribed to His holy self, a clarification in which there is no obscurity in any part. This produced His saying, as a rebuke to the one who wishes to nullify it and to conceal it: ﴿None disputes﴾, that is, contends, argues, and wishes to turn the matters to his own purpose, ﴿concerning the signs﴾, and the place of the pronoun is made explicit to magnify the signs, so He said: ﴿of Allah﴾, that is, in nullifying the lights of the Supreme King, encompassing the attributes of perfection, which indicate like the sun that the final return is to Him, by deceiving himself with doubt about that because of a resemblance toward which he inclines, or by another who casts doubt upon him, or in something other than that of what the Exalted has informed of. ﴿Except those who disbelieve﴾, that is, they covered the mirrors of their intellects and the lights of their insights, as a deception upon themselves and a confusion upon others.

Since it became established that the Gathering is unavoidable, and that Allah, the Exalted, is capable of every capability, (p-8) because He has no partner and He encompasses all the attributes of perfection, there followed from that His saying: ﴿So let not their movement through the lands deceive you﴾, that is, their moving about with trade, profits, armies, troops, and the worldly fortune that comes to them, ﴿through the lands﴾. For the act of turning about by the heart happens only through subjugation and dominance, so you might suppose, because of Our giving them respite, that they are upon the truth, or that someone protects them from Us. There must be, before long, their becoming near to Us, humbled and abased. Their delay is only so that the Book may reach its appointed term.

When He forbade being deceived by what no one has the power to avert from himself except through support from God, He gave a reason that realizes the meaning of the prohibition: that the reversal of fortune and what it produces cannot validly be relied upon, such that everyone who heard these two verses would be led to renounce it. He said, pointing by the feminine form of the verb to their weakness in resisting and their collapse when confronted, even though they were at the height of strength compared with their fellow human beings: ﴿Denied﴾. Since their denial was great and its time was ancient, while the time before it was short compared with what came after, and the affliction against them was prolonged, He made it encompass all of time, and said, without any restriction: ﴿before them﴾. Since the people at the time of Noah, peace be upon him, were one party, gathered upon one matter and one comprehensive tongue, He said: ﴿the people of Noah﴾, meaning that they were at the height of strength and capacity to carry out what they attempted, and they were one party that nothing had divided. Since the people after them had multiplied, and the differences of languages and religions had divided them, and since in some contexts a collective designation carries a force that a detailed one does not, He said: ﴿and the factions﴾, meaning the scattered nations, who cannot be counted. He indicated the closeness of the time of disbelief to the deliverance from drowning by His words: ﴿after them﴾.

Since denial alone would have been sufficient as harm, this shows that they added to it by exceeding in hostility through obstinate opposition. He placed the intent to destroy first, because it is the first thing an enemy desires; if he is unable to achieve it, he descends to what is less than it. So He said: ﴿Every nation plotted﴾, meaning of the factions mentioned, ﴿against their messenger﴾, meaning the one We sent to them. Since seizing signifies overpowering, subjugation and belittling accompanied by anger, He said: ﴿to seize him﴾. Since the wording in this manner indicates that they were unable to seize him, He mentioned that they expended their effort in contending by other means, and He said, omitting the object for generality: ﴿and they disputed by falsehood﴾, meaning by a matter that has no reality and has in itself nothing but vanishing, as Quraysh and those who joined them from the Arabs do. Then He explained the reason for their disputing, saying: ﴿that they might refute﴾, meaning that they might slip and thereby remove ﴿by it the truth﴾, meaning the established truth whose stability admits no stratagem for its removal.

Since it is known to everyone of understanding that the doer of such a thing is defeated, and that his action brings about the anger of the one who sent the messenger, He turned the speech to the speaker, to repel harm and to indicate the intensity of anger, and stripped it of the appearance of majesty in order to belittle them, saying: ﴿So I seized them﴾, meaning I destroyed them while they were humbled, in anger against them and as a humiliation to them. Since His seizing was great, He indicated His greatness by the fact that He is worthy to be asked about His condition, to increase its magnitude in the strength of its grip, the speed of its destruction, and its breaking of customary patterns, so He said: ﴿Then how was My punishment﴾. Whoever looks at their dwellings and traces their remains will come upon some of what we have indicated and drawn attention to. He omitted the first-person possessive ya' to indicate that the least of His punishment, by the least degree of relation, suffices for the intended meaning, even if the one punished were all of mankind.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 6:

Since the construction was: "Thus the Word of God became due against them for their seizing [them] because of this disputing, that they are the companions of the Fire which they disputed about," He joined to it His saying: ﴿And thus﴾, that is, and in the manner that Our Word became due against them with seizing, so that they could not escape its rights, ﴿has the Word become due﴾ through seizing and punishment, ﴿the Word of your Lord﴾. He turned the speech toward the attribute of benevolence, gently and as good tidings to him (ﷺ) of kindness toward his people, so He said: ﴿your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is benevolent to you in every kind of benevolence, so He will not leave your enemies [unpunished].

Since the context concerns disputing in falsehood, which is turning the opponent away from his correct belief, and that is concealing the true proof and confusing it, the situation was more deserving of expression by disbelief (kufr), whose meaning is concealment. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: ﴿against those who disbelieved﴾, that is, those who committed disbelief at some time. All of them are alike, these Arabs and others, because the cause of destruction is one, namely denial (takdhib), which indicates that whoever is characterized by it is created for the Fire. Then He made ﴿that they are the companions of the Fire﴾ a substitute (badal) for "the Word," that is, whoever disbelieved at any time is deserving of the Fire in the Hereafter just as he is deserving of seizing in this world, and God does not care about him at all. Whoever is overtaken by mercy through repentance is saved, and whoever is ruined by the curse through persistence perishes.

When he had explained the enmity of the disbelievers toward the prophets, peace be upon them, and their followers, may Allah be pleased with them, with His words ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah﴾ [Ghafir: 4] and what follows it, and this was an upsetting, grieving, and painful matter, He concluded it by explaining the rights of the word of punishment against them, as consolation for those who opposed them, may He be glorified. He increased their consolation by expanding their hearts and strengthening their hearts through explaining the guardianship of the angels brought near to them, given that they are the most special of creation in the presence of Him, may He be glorified, and the nearest of them to the place of His intimacy and the seat of His holiness. He also explained the rights of His mercy for those who believe, through the prayer of the people of His presence for them. So He said, or it may be said: when He explained the rights of the word of punishment, it was as if it had been said: "Then how is salvation?" It was said: through bringing faith into existence with repentance from disbelief, so that its position is fit for intercession concerning it from the people of the exalted presence, (p-12) and He will forgive him what he committed of disbelief if he repents. So He said, showing the nobility of faith and its excellence: ﴿Those who bear the Throne﴾. They are the ones brought near, and they are four, as will be mentioned, Allah willing, in al-Haqqah. When the Resurrection comes, they will be eight. Whether they are individual beings or ranks is a matter of discussion that will be mentioned, Allah willing. ﴿And those around it﴾: they are all the angels and others, whom Allah may have willed to be encompassing it, as was mentioned in the verse before it. ﴿And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne﴾ [al-Zumar: 75], meaning circling around it. This expression therefore conveyed explicit mention of all of them along with depicting the greatness.

Since it might occur to the mind that He, may He be glorified, needs them to carry His Throne, or needs the Throne, or anything else, He alerted through the glorification (tasbih) that He is free of need of everything, and that what is meant by the Throne, the bearers, and the like is the display of His admonition to us through a sensible likeness, as an act of gentleness toward us, descending to what our minds can contain and our understandings can bear. So He said, reporting about the subject and what is joined to it: ﴿They glorify﴾, meaning they declare Him free of every blemish of deficiency, bringing about His transcendence, may He be glorified, ﴿with the praise﴾. He turned the speech to their pronoun, informing that all are His servants, from the higher and lower, the near and far, and existing under His control and dominion, His beneficence and His compelling. So He said: ﴿of their Lord﴾, meaning through the encompassing of the Benefactor toward them with attributes of perfection.

Since He, may He be exalted, is hidden and no one encompasses Him in knowledge, He indicated that they, despite being the people of the presence, are behind the veil of pride and the mantles of greatness, with no difference between them (p-13) in this and those who are in the lowest earth, through His saying: ﴿and believe in Him﴾, because faith is only through the unseen. Since they, because of their nearness, are the most fearful of creation, for fear is in proportion to nearness to those presences, they are more fearful than the people of the seventh heaven, and the people of the seventh heaven are more fearful than the people of the sixth heaven, and so on. They had known, from Allah's exaltation of the human species, what others did not know, because He, may He be glorified, commanded them to exalt it through what He specifically singled out for prostration. Since drawing near to the king is among the closest means of approach to him through drawing near to his loved ones, He, may He be glorified, alerted to all of that through His saying: ﴿and they seek forgiveness﴾, meaning they ask for the erasure of sins, both their essences and their traces.

Since association in faith is stronger than unity in lineage, He said, indicating that this attribute must be the most compelling reason for counsel and the most prompting cause for sincere compassion: ﴿for those who believe﴾, meaning those who brought this reality into being, because of the brotherhood of faith between them and its kinship, even if their kinds differ in the reality of their composition, and even if after that some defect occurs from them that makes the word binding upon them, were it not for pardon, ﴿and they did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾ [al-Zumar: 67], ﴿and He pardons much﴾ [al-Shura: 30]. "No one will enter Paradise by his deed alone." When He mentioned their seeking forgiveness, He explained their expression of it through His saying: ﴿Our Lord﴾, meaning O You who have been good to us with faith and other things. Since the intent is to explain the breadth of His mercy (p-14), may He be glorified, and His knowledge, and that this is a matter the intellects cannot bear, He shifted to the style of specification (tamyiz), alerting to that, along with what it contains of stirring the listener and arousing his desire, moving from vagueness to clarification. So He said: ﴿You have encompassed all things﴾. Then He explained the aspect of this encompassing through His saying, as a specification transferred from the subject: ﴿in mercy﴾, meaning Your mercy, that is, by bringing him into existence from non-existence and what is beyond that. ﴿And in knowledge﴾, meaning Your knowledge has encompassed them. So whoever You honor, it is from knowledge of what You have brought upon him of what requires humiliation or honor.

Since it belongs to Him, may He be glorified, to do what He wills, such as punishing the obedient, bestowing bliss upon the disobedient, and other things, they said, alerting to that: ﴿So forgive those who repent﴾, meaning those who returned to You from their sins by Your mercy toward them, by erasing their essences and traces, so there is no punishment, no reproach, and no mention of them. ﴿And follow﴾, meaning they obliged themselves, despite its crookedness, to adhere to ﴿Your path﴾, the straight one in which there is no confusion. Since forgiveness may be for some sins, and since He, may He be exalted, has the right to punish one who has no sin and to punish one whose sin He has forgiven, they said: ﴿and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire﴾, meaning make between them and it a protection, by obligating them to uprightness, and completing Your blessing upon them, for You have promised whoever is like that this, and Your word does not change, though it is permissible for You to do what You will.

(p. 15) Since deliverance from punishment does not necessarily entail reward, they said, repeating the attribute of beneficence to increase their tenderness in seeking grace: ﴿Our Lord﴾, meaning, O You who are good to us by granting success to our beloved ones, who took delight in sharing with us in Your servants through the heart, the tongue, and the limbs, ﴿and admit them to Gardens of Eden﴾, meaning a dwelling in which there is no hindrance. Since they knew that He, glory be to Him, is under no obligation to anyone and that nothing from Him is ugly, they drew attention to this by saying ﴿which You have promised them﴾, with added flattery and gentleness in urging, and in admitting them for the sake of Your employing them in righteous deeds.

Since a person does not find pleasure in a blessing unless his beloved ones share it with him, those who had shared with him in worship, they said, putting first the one most deserving of honor: ﴿and whoever is righteous among their fathers﴾. Then they followed with those most closely attached to the heart, saying: ﴿and their spouses and their offspring﴾. Since the doer of this among us may perhaps be ascribed humiliation or foolishness, and may perhaps be unable to forgive a person because of the multitude of opponents, they gave a reason, stressing it in order to refute the unbelievers' ascription of might to others, such as their naming of al-'Uzza (the Mighty): ﴿Indeed, You are﴾, meaning You alone, ﴿the Mighty﴾, so You forgive whom You will without being ascribed to weakness, ﴿the Wise﴾, so every act of Yours is in its most perfect place. For this reason, no one is able to annul it or diminish it.

(p-١٦) Since a person may be forgiven and honored, and since he may have in him some traits that at times lead him to commit deficient acts, they prayed for them to be made perfect, saying: ﴿And protect them from evil deeds﴾, meaning: make between them and evil deeds a protection, by purifying them from the dispositions that lead to these deeds, through purifying the hearts by removing everything disliked in them, or by forgiving these deeds for them and not repaying them for them. They magnified this purity, encouraging the soul in this world to adhere to it by suppressing the souls and extinguishing worldly desires, saying: ﴿And whoever You protect from evil deeds﴾, meaning: its consequences entirely, ﴿on that Day﴾, meaning: the Day when You admit one group to Paradise and another group to the Fire, which is caused by evil deeds; or the Day when Paradise is brought near to the God-fearing and Hellfire is made visible to the deviators. ﴿Then You have indeed had mercy on him﴾, meaning: the complete mercy, such that nothing else deserves to be called mercy alongside it, for the completeness of bliss is not achieved except through it, since envy and hatred disappear, and one is saved from the Fire by avoiding evil deeds. For this reason they said: ﴿And that﴾, meaning: this very great matter, ﴿is﴾, meaning: by itself, ﴿the great triumph﴾. So the verse is of al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one element is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, and vice versa): it mentions the entry into the gardens first as an indication of the omitted rescue from the Fire second, and the protection from evil deeds second as an indication of the omitted granting of success in righteous deeds first. The secret of this is to create longing for what is loved, namely the gardens, through doing what is loved, namely righteousness, and to create aversion to the fires through avoiding what is hated among deeds, namely evil. Thus he mentioned the effect first and omitted the cause, because in reality there is no cause except mercy, and he mentioned the cause second (p-١٧) in the entry into the Fire and omitted the effect.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 10:

When those who believed had been completed, the soul yearned to know what would befall their opposites. He began anew, emphasizing their denial of this calling by denying its day, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾, that is, those who committed disbelief even for an instant, ﴿will be called out to﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, with a call by which one of Allah's soldiers whom Allah wills will call out to them, or in the abode of higher blessings, that they were more favored with Allah than the poor among the believers. He emphasized his statement: ﴿Surely the aversion of Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King's aversion toward you for your forsaking [the truth], ﴿is greater than your aversion﴾, and his saying: ﴿[toward] yourselves﴾ is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿See how they lied against themselves﴾ [al-An'am: 24]. It is permissible, by way of allusion, to indicate the exaltation of the holy presence above what their act of aversion necessitated, for whoever calls someone to a matter and that person turns away from him to another, his turning away is an aversion toward the one who turned away. This aversion from them, which necessitates Allah's aversion toward them, leads them to a punishment by which they abhor themselves. Aversion is the most intense hatred. Then he mentioned the time of their aversion and its consequence upon them with his saying: ﴿when﴾, that is, at the time when, and he indicated that faith, given the clarity of its proofs, ought to be accepted from whatever caller it comes. So he put the verb into the passive form, saying: ﴿you are called to faith﴾, that is, to belief in Allah and in what came from Him, ﴿and you disbelieve﴾, that is, you commit disbelief, which is covering over the signs instead of displaying them and submitting to them. (p-18) This is the greatest of punishments in the sight of people of understanding, because whoever knows that his Lord is angry with him knows that weeping will not benefit him, intercession will not avail him, and there is no means of escaping it in any way.

When the denial of resurrection was among the greatest of their sins, and they had established the customs and tested what the decrees had brought about over the ages and periods, that every second thing must have a third, and since "giving life" was not used in common speech except for one who had been dead, He, glory be to Him, related their answer with a statement whose purpose is the acknowledgment of resurrection and a gentle appeal through confessing the sin, at a time when this would not benefit them, because its condition, which is the unseen, had passed. ﴿They will say: "Our Lord"﴾, meaning: O You who have been good to us by what preceded in the worldly abode, ﴿"You caused us to die twice"﴾. It has been said: once at the end of the terms of life in this worldly life, and the second by the swoon after resurrection, or by the sleep after the questioning in the grave. The correct view is that its explanation is the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿"How can you disbelieve in God, when you were dead and He gave you life, then He will cause you to die, then He will give you life again"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. As for the swoon, it is not death, and what is in the grave is not life so that death would follow from it. Rather it is a granting of power to speak, just as He, glory be to Him, empowered the pebbles to glorify Him, the stone to greet (with peace), the lizard to bear witness to the two testimonies, and the mare when her rider said to her "Thaby," the trace of a reply to her saying "Wathban" (a leap). And the saying of al-Baqarah: ﴿"And You gave us life twice"﴾: once in the womb, and the second by resurrection after death; or once by resurrection and the second by remaining from the swoon, or remaining in the grave. Thus we witnessed Your power over resurrection. ﴿"So we have confessed"﴾, meaning: as a consequence of that, we confessed, after the repeated giving of life, ﴿"our sins"﴾ which resulted from denying resurrection, because whoever does not fear the consequence goes to extremes in following desire. Thus that is a repentance for us. ﴿"Is there any way out?"﴾, meaning: out of the Fire, even by the least kind of exit, by returning to the worldly abode, ﴿"so that we may do righteous deeds"﴾, ﴿"from a way"﴾ so that we may take it and go out, and then there would be for us a third death and a third giving of life, to the Garden which You made the reward of those who affirmed resurrection.

When the answer was definitively "There is no way to that," he gave the reason with His words, ﴿That﴾, meaning this binding, lofty, all-prevailing decree of your eternal punishment in the Fire, as an expression of abhorrence from Him toward you, ﴿because﴾, meaning it was on account of the fact that ﴿when Allah was invoked﴾, meaning whenever the call to the Supreme King was made, even once, by any caller whatsoever, ﴿alone﴾, meaning as One judged to be unique or singular, with no partner, ﴿you disbelieved﴾, meaning this is your constant nature, and you would return to the world first. ﴿But when partnership is ascribed to Him﴾, meaning when association is brought about with Him and renewed, even as many times as the breaths taken, by any associator whatsoever, ﴿you believe﴾, meaning in the partners, and you renew that without hesitation, and from the renewal of disbelief. This implies that (p. 20) Allah's love for the human being is greater than his love for Him. This is evidenced by His granting him success in that whenever Allah alone is mentioned, he believes, but whenever another is mentioned alongside Him in a manner that leads to association, he disbelieves in that other and makes the matter entirely Allah's. ﴿So the judgment﴾, meaning it follows from the certainty that there is no return, and that the disbelievers harmed none but themselves, despite their claim to sound reason, and that its execution is such that every judgment ﴿belongs to Allah﴾, meaning the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, is exclusively His. There is no role for customs in His rulings; rather, He does whatever He wills, whether by operating in accordance with customs or by breaking them. ﴿The Most High﴾, meaning alone, exalted above having any partner. Thus he refuted the statement of Abu Sufyan on the day of Uhud, "Exalted is Hubal," and the statement of Ibn 'Arabi, one of the followers of Pharaoh, who is more lying, more ugly, and more false, when he said: "The Most High is exalted above 'from' and there is nothing but Him." Upon him be disgrace and curse, and upon whoever says his words, and upon whoever hesitates to curse him.

Since souls do not submit completely to the ruler except with exceptional greatness and antiquity of glory, he spoke in a way that combines greatness and antiquity: ﴿the Great﴾, the One to whom alone greatness is fitting. Every arrogant person is made great, and every great person who is humbled beneath the circle of His greatness and majesty is diminished. His punishment is commensurate with His majesty. How foolish is the wretch who relies on the great, for they will cling to themselves, saying what will not benefit them: ﴿Our Lord, we obeyed our masters and our elders﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 13:

When he restricted the judgment to Him, he indicated this by His words, mentioning among the signs of the higher horizons that which turns the one granted success away from his error: ﴿He it is﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿who shows you﴾, that is, by sight and by insight, ﴿His signs﴾, that is, His marks indicating His singularity in the attributes of perfection, perfecting your souls, so that ﴿He sends down from the sky water﴾, and by it He revives the earth by restoring what was crushed in it of grains, so they became crumbled after their death, by the transformation of that seed into dust with no distinction from its dust. Thus one who has been reduced to nothing, who became dust and was lost in the dust of the earth so that there is no distinction for him from it, is reminded thereby of resurrection. His natural disposition is repentance, which is returning from what he is upon of ignorance to the proof, by what He has fixed in his nature of knowledge. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and He sends down for you﴾, that is, specifically for your benefit or your harm, ﴿from the sky﴾, that is, the direction of height, which indicates the subjugation of what descends from it by His holding it back until the time of the judgment of its descent, ﴿provision﴾ for the sustaining of your bodies, from fruits and sustenance, by the sending down of water. So He, glorified is He, guides you to Himself and makes Himself beloved to you, so that you may benefit your souls, while you are hostile toward Him and ignore Him so that you harm them. ﴿And none remembers﴾ that with a complete remembrance, by what the manifest expression has pointed to, so that he may infer from it the resurrection of one whom the vermin have eaten and whose remainder has been reduced to nothing in the earth, ﴿except one who turns in repentance﴾, that is, one who has the capacity for renewal at every time to return to the proof, by being upright, inclining toward the proof wherever it inclines, for his gentleness with the proof. He is not one of rigid adherence to what he has become accustomed to, nor is he turned from it at all; he does not listen to "he said" or "it was said," even if every proof were to stand against his discourse.

When every one of the people claims that he does not deviate from the evidence, and when everyone is commanded to reflect upon the evidence and commanded to turn in repentance (inabah, returning to God) to what it points to, namely turning toward God alone, this became a cause for everyone's knowledge of tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), which necessitates belief in His complete power, which necessitates belief in resurrection. So it became a cause for their sincerity (ikhlas). Then the Exalted said, as a consequence of this: ﴿So call upon﴾, and He explicitly mentioned the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam), training the sincere in the manner of sincerity, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., the One singled out by the attributes of perfection, calling upon Him in submission and worship after repentance, after reflection on the evidence, ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, i.e., the deeds upon which the recompense falls. Whoever believes in the recompense, and believes that his Lord is free of need and accepts only what is pure, strives to purify his deeds, performing them in the utmost purity from everything that could defile them, without any trace of shirk, whether manifest or hidden, just as his object of worship is one, without any trace of deficiency.

When opposing the kind (of the disbelievers) was very severe, because of what it calls for of hostility, which necessitates contention, which necessitates taking pleasure in death, the Exalted said: ﴿Though the disbelievers dislike it﴾, i.e., the calling (upon Him) from you, ﴿the disbelievers﴾, i.e., those who cover the lights of their intellects. Sincerity is that (p-23) the servants do for their Lord the like of what He did for them, so they do not perform any act of commanding or forbidding except for His sake alone, without any purpose for themselves of bringing about some benefit or harm. This is because He, glorified be He, did for them every kindness, of creation and provision, and for their own sake alone, not for a purpose that returns to Him, glorified be He and exalted be His station, with benefit or harm. So their thanks to Him is nothing but what has preceded. However, when He, glorified be He, knew that He had permitted them to act for the sake of hoping for His reward and fearing His punishment, and did not make that a flaw in their sincerity, al-Ustadh Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri said: Were it not for His permission in that, there would not be a sincere person in the world.

(p-24) Since sincerity (al-ikhlās) can only be attained by one whom the radiance of the spirit (ishrāq al-rūḥ) lifts above the murkiness of bodies, and whose lights carry him up from the depths of the darkness of ignorance to the throne of gnosis (al-ʿirfān), then, since the Sovereign, the Judge (al-Malik al-Dayyān), becomes the hearing with which he hears, in the sense that he does not act with any of these limbs except as He, glorified is He, has commanded him, he disposes of the created beings by the leave of the Opener, the All-Knowing; hearts acquire the light of His illumination, and the dead aspirations come to life by His pure secrets. Glorified is He, indicated this, urging towards it and making it desirable, by His saying, presenting it in a manner that people can understand, and informing about an omitted subject whose estimated form is: He is ﴿the Lofty in degrees﴾. That is, none reaches His presence, which is exalted, except one who has risen through the ascending stages of worship and the steps of perfections.

Since we do not know a king except by his dominance over the throne of kingship, and the steps (durj) of every king are that by which one reaches his throne, He, glorified is He, indicated with the plural of paucity (jamʿ al-qilla) the heavens, which are below His throne, glorified is He. Then He indicated that the steps to Him cannot be counted in any way, because if we spent the lifetime of this world building steps to reach the lowest heaven, we would not arrive; so how about what is above it? Moreover, His exaltation, glorified is He, is not a matter of distance, but the exaltation of greatness and the penetrating effect of His word, before which hopes are cut off and days and nights come to an end. The one who reveals this with the most complete disclosure is His expression in ﴿asked﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 1] in the form of the final plural ﴿the ways of ascent﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 3]. Then He said, presenting to us what we know: ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾, that is, the Perfect One, of whom there is in reality no throne except Him. So He encompasses all created beings and is the substance of every inanimate and living thing, and He is exalted by His majesty and greatness above everything that occurs to minds.

Since kings issue their commands from the ranks of their great ones to those whom they have sincerely befriended, He said: ﴿He casts the Spirit﴾, that is, the One by whom spirits live (p-25) with the life of forms through spirits, ﴿by His command﴾, that is, by His speech. There is no doubt that what is cast is not the inner speech (al-kalām al-nafsī), but what indicates it, and this is what accepts descent, recitation, writing and the like. Since His command is high above every command, He indicated this with the particle of elevation, and said: ﴿upon whom He wills﴾. And since the kings we have seen are not able to raise every one of their subjects whom they wish, He drew attention to His greatness by saying: ﴿of His servants﴾. By this, together with the indication that His command is absolute and it is not permissible for anyone to object to it, and if one were to object, his objection would be too insignificant to be noticed or relied upon in any way — (this is) in refutation of their saying ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ [Ṣ: 8], since he, peace be upon him, was the sincere one among His servants; he never inclined to any of their idols for a single moment, nor turned away from the true God for the blink of an eye. Therefore He singled him out from among them with this Spirit, for which there is no spirit in existence besides it. Whoever turns to it, is sincere in its recitation, acts by what it calls to, and keeps far from what it forbids, becomes one with a living spirit that revives the dead and outshines the luminaries.

Al-Rāzī said: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ said: The life of the heart is according to what the Spirit is cast upon it. Some have cast upon them the spirit of the Message (risāla), some the spirit of Prophethood (nubuwwa), some the spirit of truthfulness (al-ṣiddīqiyya), unveiling (al-kashf) and direct witnessing (al-mushāhada), some the spirit of knowledge and gnosis, some the spirit of worship and service (p-26), and some only the spirit of life; for such a one there is no knowledge of God nor station with God, so he is dead inwardly, and his life is the animal life by which he is guided to subsistence but not to the Hereafter. End of quotation. In sum, each of these spirits is a speech for the one upon whom it is cast, an absolute freedom for his tongue with its wondrous exposition, though their utterances differ in their clarity and their handling of its great matter.

When He explained the secret of His singling out of this noble Prophet for the sending, He followed that with what adds further clarification about the fruit of the sending, and said: ﴿that He may warn﴾, that is, the one whom He, glorified is He, singled out with His Spirit. He expressed it with what the classification of people requires, which is the aim of the surah, of gathering; and He removed the illusion of one who might think that meeting Him is impossible because of His elevation of degrees and the lowliness of others' degrees: ﴿of the Day of Meeting﴾, that is, the Day which none deserves to be described as the meeting in reality except Him, because the first and the last, the people of the heavens and the earth, meet in it, and none of them has any way of escaping his adversary without a decision in accordance with justice. To this meaning points the reading of Ibn Kathīr with the affirmation of the yāʾ in both states, and it is very clear in the singling out of the two parties, the most fortunate and the most wretched, for it is a meeting that has no end. The reading of the majority (al-Jumhūr), with the elision in both states, points to the meeting of these two parts with each other (p-27), for, God knows best, it seldom happens until they separate by command, each to his abode: the most fortunate without reckoning, and the most wretched for whom no weight is set up. The affirmation in the standing place (al-mawqif), as opposed to the joining, indicates the intermediate matter, which is for those who remain, their meeting extends until the time of retaliation between some of them and others.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 16:

When that made clear the absence of any screen from houses or mountains, or trees or hills, or anything else of the various kinds of shade, he drew attention to it in His saying, repeating mention of the Day because it is more terrifying for them: ﴿The Day they will come forth,﴾ meaning, both in their outward and inward selves, ﴿with nothing concealed from Allah.﴾ That is, they have emerged with no covering whatsoever in it.

Since it was known to them that the absence of a screen is something known, He made them proceed according to what they are accustomed to, and He expressed it with a phrase that encompasses all of that, saying, beginning a new statement in answer to one who thinks that something might be hidden from Him by a screen, magnifying the matter by mentioning the Greatest Name: ﴿Nothing of them is hidden from Allah,﴾ meaning, the One encompassing in knowledge and power, ﴿neither their essences nor their meanings, whether they appear or conceal themselves on this Day or at any other time.

Since it is the continuous custom that when a great king sends his army against those whose rebellion and obstinacy toward him has lasted long, and they conquer them and bring them before him, his herald calls out to them while they stand before him, their silence imposed by his awe and their humiliation brought about by his greatness, with a tongue that he speaks or the tongue of his state, with what makes them weep, rebukes them, saddens them over what passed of their disobedience, and makes them regret, He says: ﴿"To whom belongs the Dominion today?"﴾ meaning, O you who used to act as one who thinks no one is able to overpower him, so they answer with the tongue of state or of speech, as one of those who spoke said:

*The age was silent for a long time about them,*
*until it made them weep tears when it spoke.*

﴿"To Allah"﴾ meaning, the One to whom belong all attributes of perfection. Then He indicated this by His saying: ﴿"the One, the Irresistible."﴾ meaning, the One for whom it is impossible to have a second, by partnership, division, or otherwise; ﴿the Subduer﴾ meaning, the One who overpowers whomever He wills, this attribute being repeated constantly and eternally, because of what is established of His absolute self-sufficiency through His true oneness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 17:

When he had informed of the submission of every soul to the severing of all means, he informed them of what would increase their terror and stir their desire and dread, and this is the result of His being sovereign (taqaddur bil-mulk). He said: ﴿Today every soul will be recompensed﴾, i.e., be requited and repaid. He made the verb passive (buniya lil-maf'ul) because what is being made to desire and dread is the recompense itself, and to show how easy it is for Him, glorified be He. ﴿Every soul﴾: not one soul will be left out, because His knowledge has encompassed them, His power has surrounded and overtaken them, and His wisdom has prevented the neglect of any one of them.

Since the context is that of the King (al-malik), and dominion (al-qahr) requires recompense and reliance on acquisition (al-kasb), which is the locus of the obligation (al-taklif) through command and prohibition, and requires examining causes, for that is the way of a king, He said, expressing acquisition with the particle bi (ba' of causation): ﴿for what﴾, i.e., by reason of what ﴿it has earned﴾, i.e., what it did, while it supposes that it will be repaid in equal measure, by the very measure with which it was measured out to it.

Since causation conveys justice, increase would be without cause. He said, giving the reason and negating the kind of oppression some of them practised upon others in the world: ﴿No injustice﴾, i.e., in any form whatsoever ﴿today﴾. And since accounting for creatures through requital is a matter that cannot ordinarily be controlled or its retention and binding be easily managed, how much more so when exact equality is intended even in weights of pearls and less than that:

"By a scale of justice that does not deviate by a barleycorn, / for which it has a witness from itself, not one who needs support."

The souls were distressed from fear of prolongation, so He lightened it for them by His saying, informing them that His affairs are other than what they are accustomed to, and for this reason He emphasized and magnified it by stating the Greatest Name: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, i.e., the one of complete power and all-encompassing knowledge, ﴿is swift in reckoning﴾, i.e., most extreme in speed therein, not occupied by the reckoning of one person from the reckoning of another at the time of that other's reckoning, nor is He preoccupied by one matter from another, because He does not need to make an effort at counting, nor does He need to consult a book, nor anything. Thus in this there is both hope for both groups and warning, because the wrongdoer fears the swiftness of seizure with punishment, and the believer hopes for the swiftness of expansion with reward.

When this was complete in this awe-inspiring manner, and the Day of Resurrection has names that indicate its terrors according to its stations and conditions, among them: the Day of Resurrection (yawm al-ba'th), which is clear; the Day of Encounter (yawm al-talaq), for the reason already mentioned; the Day of Mutual Loss (yawm al-taghabun), because most of those in it will lose; and the Day of the Imminent (yawm al-azifa), because of its nearness and the swiftness of its seizing. It was as if it were said, addressing the Prophet ﷺ: "And warn them of the one from whom We sent down this Great Spirit by Our command, so warn them of what has passed of the Day of Encounter and what follows it." Then He joined to it His saying, to add to the explanation of its terror, informing that it is near even though it is established, and the encounter is established in it, as a warning against Iblis's embellishing of desires and his encouraging of them by procrastinating repentance: ﴿And warn them﴾, that is, these who turn away with the aversion of one who does not consider the possible, ﴿of the Day of the Imminent﴾, that is, the state that is approaching, hastening, extremely swift, together with the narrowness of time and the evil of life for most people. It is the Resurrection. He repeated its mention in the warning, explicitly and allusively, to magnify its terror and exalt its matter.

When He mentioned the Day, He magnified its matter by what occurs in it of hardships, so He said: (p-31) ﴿When the hearts﴾, that is, of everyone present. Since this terror is of a strange, inward kind, He expressed it with "ladā" (at, close by), saying: ﴿are at the throats﴾, that is, the throats of those gathered in it, except whom Allah wills. It is the plural of hunjur, and it is the windpipe in form and meaning. He means that they have moved from their places, rising up from the abundance of terror, until they almost come out, and their places in the hearts have become empty air. The hearts were stuck, like a choking obstruction: they neither return to their resting places so that they might rest, nor come out so that they might die.

Since the discourse, though apparently about the hearts, is in fact about their owners, He gave it the form of the plural used for rational beings. What adds beauty is that the hearts are the seat of restraint, and the soundness and corruption of the whole body depend on them. He has attributed to them what is attributed to rational beings, saying: ﴿restraining [their anger]﴾, that is, full of fear, terror and grief, silent, distressed, the passages of their breaths blocked, and all their senses seized.

Since it is known that this anguish is only from fear of the Judge of that Day, and since it is customary that friendships and intercessions benefit on such a day, He said, beginning a new statement: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no intimate friend﴾, that is, those deeply immersed in wrongdoing among them, ﴿nor any intercessor (shafi') who is obeyed﴾, that is, a true friend in their affection, concerned with their affairs, removing their distresses. Ibn Burjan said: "The ḥamīm is boiling hot water, intensely hot; the close friend is named after it because he protects his close one with anger, and anger is a heat that arises in the heart and goes out to the face, so it reddens and the veins swell, and he becomes furious with rage." ﴿Nor any intercessor who is obeyed﴾ means: they have no intercessor at all, because an intercessor knows that if he interceded he would not be obeyed, so he does not benefit. Some of the near ones may intercede for some of them due to a sign in them by which a resemblance arises, making them seem to be among those deserving intercession, so it is pointed out to him that they are not of that kind, and he disowns them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 19:

When intercession (shafa'ah) only takes place and benefits on condition that the one for whom intercession is sought is free of sin, either by acknowledging what is attributed to him and giving it up, or by offering an excuse for it, and since this is something that among created beings operates only on the outward appearance, for this reason they sometimes made mistakes concerning one whose inner state, had they known it, they would not have accepted intercession for him, the Exalted explained what preceded by His knowledge, that the one for whom intercession is sought is not fit to receive intercession on his behalf, because His knowledge encompasses everything, so He said: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾. Since the context here is for the purpose of emphasizing that the knowledge of the Exalted encompasses every universal and particular, it is known that the situation calls for the plural of abundance, and that He did not turn away from it to the plural of paucity (jam' al-qillah) except to point out that His knowledge of the many is, like His knowledge of the few, all equally easy for Him; so the many is in His sight few in this respect. Therefore He said: ﴿the eyes﴾, meaning their treachery, which is the most hidden of the outward actions, making the treachery an intensification in the description, and it is the signaling with the eye. (p-33) Abu Hayyan said: "Whoever winks, nods, or glances, one understands from it what is intended" — end of quote.

This is done by performing an act that contradicts the outward appearance. When he mentioned the most hidden of the outward actions, he followed it with the most hidden of what is within the heart, so He said: ﴿and what the breasts conceal﴾, meaning from the one for whom intercession is sought, in the view of the one to whom it is addressed, and other than that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 20 (part 1 of 2):

Since pardoning a wrongdoer who does not turn back from his wrongdoing would be a deficiency, because there would be no wisdom in it, He expressed Himself with the greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam) in a circumstantial clause, saying: ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning, while the One characterized by all attributes of perfection [is the one who] ﴿judges with truth﴾, meaning with what is established and whose negation is not valid at all. So if He were to judge concerning one whom He knows is not worthy of intercession for him by accepting the intercession, He would negate the truth and establish falsehood, thereby contradicting that perfection. ﴿And those whom they invoke﴾, meaning the wrongdoers, according to the reading of the majority; and "wa-ayyuha al-zalimun" (O you wrongdoers), according to the reading of Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir, with a variant from Ibn Dhakwan, in direct address for the purpose of disparagement. Since the ranks below His greatness, glory be to Him, cannot be enumerated and nothing can encompass them all, He affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿besides Him﴾, meaning other than Him. It is known that they are His creatures, so they are below His rank, because they are under His subjugation. ﴿Do not judge anything﴾ of things at all, let alone judge what opposes His ruling. So nothing prevents Him from judging with truth, and there is no reason to accept intercession for one whom He knows to be deeply entrenched (p-34) in wrongdoing, from which he does not separate.

When He had informed that their associates have no action, and that the command belongs to Him alone, He gave the reason for that, saying, warning against treachery and other evils and encouraging every good, emphasizing, because their actions imply denial of that: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, with this expression because the context is to belittle their associates and to show that they are in the utmost deficiency. ﴿He is﴾, meaning He alone. When He mentioned what is unseen, He described Him with the most manifest of manifest attributes, saying: ﴿the All-Hearing﴾, meaning of everything that can be heard, ﴿the All-Seeing﴾, meaning with sight and knowledge, of everything that can be seen and known. So their associates have no perception at all, nor does anything other than Him have true perception. Whoever has no perception and no judgment, it is established that the command belongs to Him alone. Therefore the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them, and no intercession will be accepted for any of them after the general intercession, which is specific to our Prophet (ﷺ), and which is the praised station (al-maqam al-mahmud) that all the first and the last will envy him for. For every person will hold back from it until the matter reaches him (ﷺ), and he says: "I am for it, I am for it." Then he goes to the place he was permitted to go, and intercedes, and Allah, exalted is He, accepts his intercession. Then He, glory be to Him, judges between the creatures so that each one goes to his abode: his Paradise or his Fire. Al-Bukhari and Muslim, the two Shaykhs, related from Abu Hurayra (p-35), may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at a feast, and he lifted to him the foreleg, which he liked, and took a bite from it, and said:

"I am the master of the people on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know why? Allah gathers the first and the last in one plain, and the one who looks sees them, and the caller makes them hear, and the sun draws near to them, and people reach such distress and anguish that they cannot bear or endure it. People say: 'Do you not see what you are in and what has reached you? Will you not look to one who will intercede for you with your Lord?' Some of the people say to others: 'Your father is Adam'... [and he mentioned their asking of him], the great prophets, and each one refers them to the next, until 'Isa (peace be upon him) says: 'Go to Muhammad (ﷺ).' Then the Prophet (ﷺ), when they come to him, says: 'I am for it,' and he goes and prostrates beneath the Throne."" This is also related from other than Abu Hurayra, from Anas and other Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. But I have not found in it the explicit mention of the general intercession after he (ﷺ) raises his head from prostration, except in what al-Bukhari related in the Book of Zakat in his Sahih, in the chapter "He who asks people excessively," from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the sun will draw near on the Day of Resurrection until the sweat reaches to the middle of the ear. While they are in that state, they seek help from Adam, then from Musa, then from Muhammad, and he intercedes so that judgment may be made among the creatures. He walks until he takes hold of the ring of the door, and on that day Allah will raise him to a praised station, which all the assembled people will praise." Likewise in what Abu Ya'la related in his Musnad, he said: "Amr ibn al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad related to us: Abu 'Asim al-Dahhak ibn Mukhallad related to us: Abu Rafi' Isma'il ibn Rafi' related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from a man of the Ansar, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) related to us while he was with a group of his companions, and he said: "When Allah, blessed and exalted, finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the Trumpet, and mentioned blowing into it for death, then for resurrection, then He mentioned the gathering..."' — and it is a very long hadith, until he said: "Then they will stand in one station, the length of seventy years, no one will look at you, nor will judgment be given among you. So you will weep until the tears are exhausted, then you will weep blood, and you will sweat until that reaches your mouths or your chins. Then you will cry out and say: 'Who will intercede for us with our Lord, so that He may judge between us?' You will say: 'Who is more worthy of that than your father Adam? Allah created him with His hand, breathed into him of His spirit, and spoke to him directly.' So you will come to Adam and ask him for that, but he will refuse and say: 'I am not the one for that.' Then they will seek the prophets, prophet after prophet, each time they come to a prophet he refuses them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Until you come to me. So I will go until I come to the al-Fahs, and I will fall down prostrate (p-37)." Abu Hurayra said: "O Messenger of Allah! What is al-Fahs?" He said: "In front of the Throne. Until Allah sends to me an angel who takes hold of my arm and lifts me up, and says to me: 'O Muhammad!' I say: 'Yes, my Lord!' He says, and He knows best: 'What is your matter?' I say: 'O my Lord, You promised me, so grant me intercession for Your creation, and judge between them.' He says: 'I have granted you intercession. I will come to you and judge between you.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "So I return and stand with the people. While we are standing, we hear a tremendous sound from the heaven. The inhabitants of the lowest heaven descend, like those on earth of the jinn and mankind, until when they draw near the earth, the earth is illuminated by their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.' Then the inhabitants of the second heaven descend, like those of the angels who descended, and like the jinn and mankind, until when they draw near the earth, the earth is illuminated by their light, and they take their ranks, and we say to them: 'Is our Lord among you?' They say: 'No, but He is coming.' Then they descend in proportion to that multiplication, until the Almighty, blessed and exalted, descends in shadows of clouds, and the angels carry His Throne that day, eight of them, and that is the day of four..." — until he said: "Then Allah places His Kursi (Footstool) wherever He wills of His earth, then He calls out with His voice and says: 'O assembly of jinn and mankind! I have been silent toward you since the day of your creation until this day of yours. I hear your words, and I see your deeds. So be silent for Me, for it is only your deeds and your records that are read to you (p-38). Whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame none but himself.' Then Allah commands Hell, and a bright dark neck emerges from it. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, says: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you should not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy﴾ [Yasin: 60] ﴿And that you worship Me; this is a straight path﴾ [Yasin: 61] ﴿And he had already led astray from among you a great multitude. Did you not then use reason?﴾ [Yasin: 62] ﴿This is Hell, which you were promised﴾ [Yasin: 63] — or 'with which you were lying' — Abu 'Asim doubted, ﴿And stand apart today, O criminals﴾ [Yasin: 59]. Then the Fire is called, and the nations kneel, and you see every nation kneeling, every nation called to its book, and He judges between His creation." He recounted it, and it is very long. Then he mentioned the Sirat (bridge) and some special intercessions for the people of Paradise, mentioning their entry into Paradise, then that they intercede for some of the people of the Fire, until he said: "Then Allah permits intercession, and there remains no prophet or martyr except that he intercedes." Until he said: "Then Allah, mighty and majestic, says: 'I remain, and I am the Most Merciful of the merciful.' Then Allah puts His hand into Hell and brings out from it those whom no one else can count." 

Ibn Hibban related in his Sahih, and al-Mundhiri said: "I know of no flaw in its chain," from Hudhayfa, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim (peace be upon him) will say on the Day of Resurrection: 'O Lord!' The Lord, majestic and exalted, will say: 'Here I am, at Your service!' Ibrahim will say: 'O Lord, my son has been burned!' Then Allah says: 'Bring out from the Fire whoever has in his heart an atom's weight or a barley grain of faith.'" 

Al-Hakim related and said: "Authentic according to the condition of Muslim and Ahmad ibn Mani'": "A man meets his father on the Day of Resurrection, and he says: 'O father! What kind of son was I to you?' He says: 'The best of sons.' He says: 'Are you obeying me today?' He says: 'Yes.' He says: 'Take hold of my garment.' So he takes hold of his garment, then he sets out until he comes to Allah, while He is showing some of the creation. He says: 'O My servant! Enter through whichever gates of Paradise you wish.' He says: 'O my Lord, my father is with me, for You promised me that You would not disgrace me.' So He turns away from him and judges among the creatures, and shows them. Then He looks at him and says: 'O son of Adam! Enter through whichever gates of Paradise you wish.' He says: 'O my Lord, my father is with me, for You have promised me that You would not disgrace me.' He said: 'Then Allah transforms his father into a hyena, ḍabʿan amdhara aw amjara' — Abu Ja'far, one of the narrators of Ibn Mani', was in doubt — 'then he takes hold of his nose and says: "This is your father." He says: "He is not my father," and he is thrown into the Fire."' It is in al-Bukhari in the chapters on the Prophets and in the Tafsir of al-Shu'ara' with the wording: "Ibrahim (peace be upon him) meets his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and on Azar's face is dust and dark gloom. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) says to him: 'Did I not tell you: do not disobey me?' His father says to him: 'Today I will not disobey you.' Ibrahim says: 'O Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day they are raised. What disgrace could be greater than my father being far away?' Allah, exalted is He, says: (p-40) 'I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.' Then it is said to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'Look at what is under your feet.' He looks, and behold, there is a dhīkh (the male of the hyena), covered in filth. It is seized by its hind legs and thrown into the Fire."

Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili and al-Hakim related, and al-Hakim said: "Authentic according to the condition of the two Shaykhs," from Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A man will surely take hold of his father's hand on the Day of Resurrection, and the Fire will cut him off, wanting to enter him into Paradise. He said: Then it will be called out: 'Paradise is not entered by a polytheist. Indeed Allah has forbidden Paradise to every polytheist.' He said: Then he says: 'O Lord! My father!' Then he will be transformed into an ugly form and a foul smell, and he will leave him. So the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to think that it was Ibrahim (peace be upon him)."

The two Shaykhs and others related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivering a sermon from the pulpit, saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 20 (part 2 of 2):

"You will be gathered to Allah barefoot, naked and uncircumcised (ghurl), as We began the first creation, We will repeat it. That is a promise binding upon Us; indeed, We will be doing it." Hear this: the first of creation to be clothed will be Ibrahim, peace be upon him. Hear this: men from my community will be brought forward and taken to the left side. I will say, "My Lord, my companions!" And it will be said, "You do not know what they innovated after you." So I will say what the righteous servant said: ﴿And I was a witness over them while I remained among them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117], up to his words: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 118]."

al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it in similar wording. Similar to what 'Isa, peace be upon him, said is the saying of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, as Allah related it about him: ﴿So whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Ibrahim: 36]. Muslim, in the Book of Faith (al-Iman) of his Sahih, and al-Nasa'i, in his Tafsir, narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ recited the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, concerning Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people. So whoever follows me is of me﴾ [Ibrahim: 36], to the end of the verse. And 'Isa, peace be upon him, said: ﴿If You punish them, indeed they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 118]. Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my community! O Allah, my community! O Allah, my community!" And he wept. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad" — and your Lord knows best — "and ask him what makes him weep." So Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and asked him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ informed him of what he had said, and He knows best. Allah said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad and say: Indeed We will satisfy you concerning your community and We will not grieve you."

The Two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated in the Book of the Basin (al-Hawd) and the Book of Trials (al-Fitan), and Muslim in the Virtues of the Prophet ﷺ, from Sahl ibn Sa'd and Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "I am your forerunner at the Basin (al-Hawd). Whoever passes by it drinks, and whoever drinks from it will never thirst again. There will come to me people whom I recognize and who recognize me, and then a barrier will be placed between me and them." Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, added: "I will say, 'They are of me!' It will be said, 'You do not know what they innovated after you.' So I will say: Far away, far away, to the one who changed after me."

Muslim and Ibn Majah narrated, and this is his wording, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said" — and he mentioned his sermon at the Hajj — then said: "Hear this: I am your forerunner at the Basin, and I will boast of you before the nations. Do not blacken my face. Hear this: some people will be rescued by me, and some people will be prevented from me. I will say, 'My Lord, my companions, my companions!' And He will say: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'"

The wording of Muslim: "I am your forerunner at the Basin, and I will surely contend with some people, then I will surely overcome them. So I will say, 'My Lord, my companions!' And it will be said: 'You do not know what they innovated after you.'"

Muslim narrated from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say while he was among his companions: 'I am at the Basin, watching who among you will come to me. By Allah, men will be cut off from me, and I will surely say, "My Lord, from me and from my community!" And He will say: "You do not know what they innovated after you." They kept turning back on their heels.'"

The Two Shaykhs narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "My community will come to me at the Basin, and I will drive people away from it as a man drives away other men's camels from his own camels." They said: "O Prophet of Allah, will you recognize us?" He said: "Yes. You will have a mark that no others have: you will come to me radiant, with white marks on your limbs from the traces of ablution. But some of you will be kept away from me, and they will not reach me. I will say, 'My Lord, these are my companions!' And an angel will answer me, saying: 'Do you know what they innovated after you?'"

In another narration: "While I was standing at the Basin, suddenly a group appeared. When I recognized them, a man came out from between me and them and said: 'Come!' I said: 'Where to?' He said: 'To the Fire, by Allah!' I said: 'What is their state?' He said: 'They turned back on their heels. I do not think any of them will be saved except like the stray camels (hamal al-ni'am), i.e., their strays. The one who is saved is few.'"

In a narration of Muslim in the Book of Ablution: "Hear this: men will surely be driven away from my Basin as a stray camel is driven away. I will call to them, 'Hear this, come!' It will be said: 'They have changed after you.' So I will say: 'Far away, far away!'"

al-Mundhiri said: The hadiths on this meaning are very numerous.

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 40, verse 21:

When He (glory be to Him) admonished them with true reports about the people of Noah and those among the disbelievers who followed them, and concluded this with a warning of what befalls the wrongdoers and the wicked in the abode of settlement, He followed it with admonition and intimidation through direct observation, by traversing the abodes and reflecting on them, with their wondrous remains, including the fortresses, palaces, and all the buildings, small and large. So He said, rebuking and affirming, and conjoining (with 'atf) to what is implied, as if to say: "Have they not taken warning from what We have told them about the earlier wrongdoers, and about those who followed them, of destruction in this world, which is linked to wretchedness in the Hereafter?" ﴿Have they not travelled﴾. Since the earlier generations were so numerous, so strong, and so powerful that no one but Allah knows them, and no human can encompass their dwellings, He drew attention to this with His words: ﴿in the land﴾, meaning: in whatever land they travelled, the land would admonish them with the signs it contains.

Since travelling is a cause of looking, He said: ﴿and see﴾, meaning, a look of reflection, as is the custom of people of insight, who claim to be the highest of them. Since the conditions observed and reflected upon were extremely strange, He drew attention to them with His words: ﴿how﴾, meaning that they are worthy of being asked about.
