(p-89) Since the sense was: "We indeed helped Moses, Our messenger, against the flashing and thundering of Pharaoh," He joined to it His words, indicating honour and mercy, emphasizing the removal of what had become fixed in souls—that the kings of this world are not overcome by the weak: ﴿And We certainly gave﴾, that is, by the might that is Ours, ﴿Moses the guidance﴾, that is, in the religion, from which it follows that he should have the final outcome, however great the vastness of the one who opposes him may be, because the one who opposes him is astray from guidance, and the astray is doomed however long the term may be. This was by means of what We gave him of prophethood and the Book.

Since prophethood was specific and the Book general, He said: ﴿And We made the Children of Israel inherit﴾, that is, by Our greatness, ﴿the Book﴾, after they had been in humiliation, that is, [the one] We sent down to him and gave him as guidance by it—and it is the Torah—a giving that is like an inheritance, which no one contests with them, and there were no people entitled to it in that time other than them, its state being...

Guidance (hudan): that is, a general clarification for everyone who follows it. Reminder (dhikra): that is, a great admonition. For people of understanding (li-ulil-albab): that is, hearts that are pure and minds that are full and healing. He mentioned Moses being given the fruit (al-thamara) and mentioned their being made inheritors of the cause (al-sabab), indicating that among them were those who gathered its fruit and were guided, and among them were those who went astray. This is a warning to those who follow, and an honouring of the prophets for the ranks of elevation they attained.

The presumed sense, after the emphatic promise of support for the messengers and their followers was stated, is: "Indeed We gave you guidance and the Book, as We gave Moses, and We will surely support you as We supported him, and even if the glaring looks and thunderous threats of your people increase, they will not overcome Pharaoh in what he had of tyranny, domination, might, authority and deceit, and none of that benefited him." Therefore its consequence is His saying: ﴿So be patient﴾ [i.e.] with their harm. For We bring things to their fullest fulfilment in their proper places, according to what We have established as the states of this world, namely the running of causes upon their means. Then He gave the reason for that in His saying, turning the speech away from the aspect of greatness, which is the axis of support, to the Name of the Essence, which comprises all perfections, the greatest of which is the carrying out of command and the truthfulness of promise: ﴿Indeed, the promise of Allah﴾ [i.e.] the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿is true﴾ [i.e.] in making your religion prevail and in strengthening your cause. You have already seen what happened to Moses, peace be upon him, with the most oppressive people of his time, and what the outcome was for him. Al-Qushayri said: patience while awaiting what is promised from the Truth is in proportion to faith and affirmation; whoever's affirmation and certainty are more complete and stronger, his patience is more perfect and more abundant.

Since this discourse has assured, through the affirmation, the attainment of the aim, and since it is a decreed matter that persistent drawing near to God elevates ranks, leading to strength in actions, He commanded him to turn away from awaiting victory and to occupy himself with refining the states so as to attain the speech, addressing the highest of creation so that those below him would be included by way of priority. So He said: ﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾, that is: and it is every complete action from which you ascend to a more complete one, and every virtuous state from which you rise to a more excellent one; this is thanks (shukr) from you, (p-91) because Allah has forgiven you what preceded of your sin and what followed, so that your community will follow your example. He named it a sin by way of the saying: "The good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those brought near [to God]."

Since He commanded him to seek forgiveness when ascending to the degrees of perfection, which overlook the seas of greatness and the wastelands of majesty, He commanded him to glorify (tanzih) God, free of any trace of deficiency, and to affirm for each rank a degree of perfection, turning the speech to the attribute of nurture and kindness, because it is among the greatest of its loci, so He said: ﴿And glorify﴾, that is: declare your Lord free of any trace of deficiency, whenever you know, by ascending the ladders of perfection, the deficiency of the created in essence and in deeds, ﴿with the praise of your Lord﴾, that is: affirming the encompassing of attributes of perfection for the One who does good to you and nurtures you. Do not occupy yourself with anything other than Him, for actions are among the causes of success. Since the context is the establishment of the Hour's coming, and the evening is more indicative of it, He placed it first, saying: ﴿in the evening and the morning﴾, for their constant alternation indicates the perfection of the one who causes them to alternate and His power to bring into existence what was non-existent, annihilated, and to restore it as it was. Among what the verse implies is an encouragement to the dawn and afternoon prayers, which are the "middle" prayer, because the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness them. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: rather it refers to the five prayers; this is related by al-Baghawi. This is because the evening (al-'ashi) begins from the decline of the sun, and the morning (al-abkar) from the break of dawn until sunrise.

(p-92) Since the command to occupy oneself during these two times is, a fortiori, a command to occupy oneself during other times, the beginning of the day is a time for working and for attending to beginnings and completions, while its end is a time for preparing for rest and the afternoon nap, with eating, drinking, and what follows from them. Occupying oneself with those things would entirely divert one from the enemies of the religion, and that would be hard on the souls. So He gave a reason that calls for persistence in deeds and for turning away from them, because their abandonment is a matter that has already been settled. Giving the reason for persisting in obedience, He said: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute﴾, meaning: those who take up enmity in order to transfer [the people of] this religion away from it to the falsehood they hold. He turned the speech to the Majesty, which indicates the utmost greatness, to belittle their status, and said: ﴿concerning the signs of Allah﴾, meaning the signs of the Supreme King, which indicate the completeness of His power, from which follows His power over the Resurrection, in whose remembrance lies the welfare of religion and of the world. ﴿Without any authority﴾, meaning without any authoritative command or sound proof of a path. ﴿Has come to them﴾. ﴿There is nothing in their breasts [except]﴾, meaning: what is in their breasts is their turning away from the right way. The mention of the breasts, rather than the hearts, [indicates] the great extent of their pride, and that it has filled the hearts and overflowed from them until it occupied the breasts, which are their dwelling places. ﴿Except pride﴾, meaning: [a turning away] from following the truth, despite its light shining and its radiance rising, [with] the desire to extinguish or conceal it. Pride is the desire for precedence, for magnification, and for leadership, and for the one who desires it to be above everyone.

(p-93) ﴿They will never attain it﴾, meaning: they will never attain its aim of nullifying the religion, out of arrogance at being under its commands. They will not attain that in any way. The religion must prevail through the victory of the Messenger and those of the believers who follow him over the People of the Book, the polytheists, and the other kinds of disbelievers. Then they will be raised up, and their enemies will be the lowest of the low, humbled and abased.

Since the beginning and end of this speech have made clear, explicitly and by allusion, what the style of the words of the Powerful, formulated for the most general of what could come to mind, conveys, namely that He, exalted is He, described Himself at the opening of the sūrah as Victorious over everything, and nothing overcomes Him, and that what they have is only the desire to be exalted and victorious, the following is a consequence of that: ﴿So seek refuge﴾, meaning: ask for protection ﴿in Allah﴾, who encompasses everything, from the evil of their arrogance, just as Moses, peace be upon him, sought refuge in Him, so that He may fulfill for you what He promised you, just as He fulfilled it for him. Then He gave the reason for that, saying: ﴿Indeed, He﴾, meaning, in accordance with what He has of inwardness, ﴿He is﴾, meaning He alone is ﴿the Hearing﴾ of everything that can be heard. Since the context is seeking refuge from the devils of mankind, who possess both outward and inward deception, He concluded with ﴿the Seeing﴾, which is fit for both sight and insight, so it encompasses the perceptible and the known. [And He concluded] the two verses of al-A'raf and Fussilat, which were preceded by [mention of] the prodding of Satan, which consists of whisperings and inner promptings, with ﴿the Knowing﴾.

(p-94) Since the greatest concern in the verse of disputation repeated from the beginning of the surah up to here was the resurrection, and the return of the servants to God through the gathering (al-hashr), so that the decisive judgment may take place therein, and the support of the prophets and their followers may be realized on the Day when the witnesses stand, He indicated His power over it by something that serves as a reason for what was negated in the verse of disputation, namely their attaining what they sought of arrogance. So He said, emphatically, treating the one who acknowledges and knows as if he were the ignorant, obstinate one, because his action contradicts his belief: ﴿The creation of the heavens﴾, that is, God's creating them, despite their greatness, their height, the abundance of their benefits and their vastness, ﴿and the earth﴾, as you see of their wonders and the abundance of their provisions, ﴿is greater﴾ in the estimation of every intelligent creature among creation, in terms of creation, ﴿than the creation of mankind﴾, that is, God's creating them, because they are a small portion of the creation of both. So it is known with certainty that the One who was able to originate it, despite its greatness, is able to restore people despite their insignificance. ﴿But most people﴾, and they are those who deny the resurrection and other matters to which power may relate and which revelation has confirmed, ﴿do not know﴾, that is, they have no knowledge at all; rather, they are like cattle, because heedlessness has overcome them and they follow their desires. So they do not infer from this the power to resurrect, just as cattle see the outward and do not perceive the inward by it. Indeed, they are lower in rank than cattle, because this kind of knowledge is extremely evident, so it is like the sensible, and whoever hesitates regarding it is inanimate.

(p-٩٥) When this analogy, which is beyond dispute and against which there is no objection or criticism, has established that the One who is able to create the great at the beginning is able to level the small by restoring it, it is also established that the creation of human beings is not based on the natures of the heavens and the earth. Otherwise they would be equal in knowledge and ignorance, in measure, form and shape, because the natures' requirement for these things is in one uniform manner with no variation, and they have no choice. Some people said that this bringing into existence belongs only to the natures, and among these is Pharaoh, whose case has passed in this surah, and whose disgrace and shame were fully exposed. He refuted this view by showing that it implies equality in whatever arises from a thing of nature, since it has no choice, yet we observe things differing. This definitely shows that they are not based on a nature [but on a choosing agent. So the sense, as the context of the verse indicates, is definitely, together with its closing with the negation of knowledge]. It then coordinates what follows with something not mentioned: ﴿And few of them reflect﴾. Thus it is established that their Creator, who differentiated among them, is able, choosing, and without partner, for the knowing and the ignorant are not equal: ﴿And not equal are﴾, that is, in any respect at all in terms of sight, ﴿the blind and the seeing﴾. This necessitates knowledge that those who differ are not based on nature, but on a choosing agent.

When He mentioned the two sensory darknesses and light, He followed them with the two non-sensory ones in a scrambled order (p-٩٦) so that the two kinds of darkness would reveal the two kinds of light, indicating that the guided one is rare to find, like pure gold among coins. So He said: ﴿And those who believe﴾, that is, who brought this truth into existence, whether it was established or not, ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, likewise, so they are doers of good. ﴿Nor the evildoer﴾, that is, the one established in evil, who disbelieved and did not do righteous deeds. The change in the conjunction occurs because the intended meaning, God knows best, is the equality [itself] between individuals of the blind and individuals of the seeing, and between the doer of good and the doer of evil. But since among the addressees there are the dull and the clever, He coordinated "the seeing" without "not," so that the apparent meaning would be the negation of equality between the two kinds, the blind and the seeing, because negating equality between individuals of kinds is subtle. He used only the conjunction "wa" with "those who believe," because it would not be coherent to intend making the blind and the seeing one group and the believer described as another group, and equality between them is negated, since there is no confusion that the described believers are like the seeing, and none of them could imagine their equality with the blind. So it is clear that what is intended is the negation of equality of the blind with the seeing, and the negation of equality of the described believer with the evildoer. "Not" was added (p-٩٧) before "the evildoer" [and he expressed it in the singular], indicating to the discerning that what is intended is the negation of equality between individuals of each kind, because that is more indicative of power and that it is by choice. This differs from the darknesses in Surah Fatir, for if "not" were left out there, someone might imagine that what is negated is equality between the blind and the seeing and the darknesses, and then the objection would arise that the darknesses are equal to them, in the sense that a darkness among them is so dense that sight cannot penetrate it, and among them is one so faint that it is called darkness only relative to bright light. The verse is an example of ihtibak (rhetorical balancing): He mentioned doing righteous deeds first as evidence of their opposite second, and the evildoer second as evidence of the doers of good first. Its secret is that He mentioned righteousness as encouragement and evil as warning.

When this has been settled in this manner of clarity, which leaves no barrier for a person to understand it and to firmly retain it in his knowledge, except his failure to remember it even in himself, the Exalted said: ﴿Little do you remember﴾, that is, the disputants, or O disputants, or people, because the one who remembers to the utmost degree, as indicated by the manifest form, is among you few. According to the reading of the Kufans with the second-person form, because it is stronger in rebuke and more indicative of anger.

Since all of this establishes the perfection of power, and what the one who has no insight among the natures imagined is negated, His saying is established with certainty: ﴿Indeed, the Hour﴾, that is, the Resurrection, about which the disputers dispute, ﴿is surely coming﴾. By My might! It is for judging with justice in comparing the evildoer and the good-doer, [because] it is not permissible in wisdom, according to anyone among creation, that one should equate a servant who does good with one who does evil. How then could one suppose this of the Most Just of judges, whom we see causing the evildoer to die while he is in the height of blessing and disobedience, and the good-doer while he is in the height of trial and obedience, and the wronged person before he has obtained redress from the wrongdoer? For this manifest reason He said: ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾, that is, there is no doubt in its coming in any way, ﴿so that I may judge in it [with justice], admitting some people into the abode of My mercy and others into My retribution﴾.

When the matter of the Hour reached a limit with no hiddenness at all, He negated faith without knowledge, so the Exalted said: ﴿But most people﴾, that is, with what is in them of al-nawS (the disquiet, i.e., oscillation and agitation), [and he observed the meaning of "most" so he used the plural, because the plural is more indicative of the intended sense and firmer in rebuke]: ﴿do not believe﴾, that is, they do not make the one who informs them of its coming secure from denial, despite the clarity of its knowledge to them. And this is due only to the obstinacy of some of them and the shortsightedness of the rest, who rely on the senses.

[p. 99] Since the implied meaning is: "Your Lord did that so that He might judge among His servants with justice, so that the doer of good enters Paradise as an act of support for him, and the evildoer enters the Fire as abandonment and humiliation for him," when His promise had appeared, that He helps His messengers and their followers in this world and in the Hereafter, and He said to all His servants, "Believe, so that I may keep you safe from the dangers of that abode," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And your Lord said﴾, meaning the Benefactor to you by guiding you and promising you support. ﴿Call upon Me﴾, meaning respond to Me by worshipping Me alone, so that you ask Me for what I have promised you of support, as an act of worship. This is the meaning of his saying ﷺ, "Supplication is worship" (ﷺ). He confined supplication to worship, whether it is by supplicating, praying, or otherwise. Whoever is a worshipper, humbly submissive to Allah Most High, whether through asking or otherwise, his worship is a supplication. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Make Me One, and I will forgive you." And on the authority of al-Thawri, it was said to him, "Supplicate," and he said, "Indeed, abandoning sins is supplication."

﴿Ast-ajib﴾ (I will respond), meaning He brings about the response in a great manner, as if He were one who seeks it with utmost desire for it.

﴿for you﴾ in this world, meaning by bringing about what you supplicated for, or removing a similar harm, or storing it for you in the Hereafter, so that the difference becomes evident between one for whom there is a supplication and one for whom there is no supplication, in this world or the Hereafter. Do not rely on what the promise has preceded, so that you abandon supplication and thus abandon the worship whose essence is supplication. "Each is made easy for what he was created for." Al-Qushayri said: "It was also said: supplication is the key to response, and its teeth are the morsel of lawful food." End of quotation. The verse has the same meaning as the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿I respond to the prayer of the supplicant when he calls upon Me; so let them respond to Me﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:186].

Since the cause of abandoning supplication is usually arrogance, it was as if it were said: "Do not abandon My supplication, lest you become arrogant." He gave the reason for it, with a warning encompassing an encouragement, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are arrogant﴾, meaning those who manifest arrogance. It indicates that by supplication is meant worship, in His saying: ﴿from My worship﴾, meaning from responding to Me in what I have called them to of worship, by disputing My signs and turning away from My supplication in all that befalls them in hardship and ease. ﴿Will enter﴾ by a promise that admits no failure ﴿Hell﴾, so it will meet them as a recompense for their arrogance, with scowling, grimacing and aversion, ﴿humiliated﴾, meaning abased, contemptible and disgraced. The verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which each part omits what is mentioned in the other): it mentioned supplication first as evidence for its omission second, and worship second as evidence for its omission first.

[p. 100] And since He also concluded this with the matter of the Hour, He increased the indication of it, and of the act by choice and wisdom, which does not permit leaving creation neglected without accounting, in an abode of reward and punishment, after perfecting the abode of action with error and correctness. So He said, giving the reason, opening with the Greatest Name, of which one cannot imagine that the One named by it [p. 101] would neglect the arrogant who are against Him, along with the completeness of His beneficence toward them.

﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿who made for you﴾, not another, ﴿the night﴾ [that is]: dark, ﴿that you may rest therein﴾, an apparent rest through sleep, which is the lesser death, and a true rest through worship, which is everlasting life; ﴿and the day as something giving sight﴾, that you may move about in it through wakefulness, which is a kind of revival in meaning. The verse is an example of *ihtibak* (a figure of speech in which two contrasting elements are mentioned, each omitting what the other supplies). Darkness is omitted first, because it is not among the favours intended in themselves, given what is indicated by "giving sight," which is what is intended from the light, the intended favour in itself. Dispersal is omitted, because it is part of what arises from the favour of sight, given what is indicated by "rest," which is the greatest purpose of the night: for repose for whoever desires it, and for worship for whoever relies on it and seeks more of it.

Since some of the disbelievers attribute the actions, as has passed, to the natures (*tabai'*, natural causes) and regard them as occurring without choice, He said, beginning a new statement or giving a reason, emphasizing: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the Lord of majesty and honour, ﴿is truly full of bounty﴾, that is, immensely great by His choice, ﴿toward mankind﴾, that is, all of them, through the alternation of night and day and the benefits they contain. When these verses reached such a degree of indication of the Oneness, the resurrection, and the negation of the matter of natures, a degree rarely found in other passages, the opponent became deserving of extreme blame for that. Thus the generalized blame of those who oppose fell in its most fitting place. A noun may be intended to mean only part of its meaning, and here the generalization was intended; so he made it explicit (by using the noun rather than a pronoun) to convey that this is what is intended, and did not use a pronoun so that the judgment would attach to the descriptive term that conveys the sense of the (*nawas*, drowsiness, a state of the spirit's lapse toward sleep) and points out that its bearer falls short of the rank of the first of the believers' ranks. Thus one knows that this kind of person is disposed to that. So He said: ﴿but most people﴾, that is, with their instability and lack of steadfastness in adhering to what is right, ﴿do not give thanks﴾, so they attribute His actions, glorified is He, to others out of ignorance, or they act in ways that strip them of the name of thankfulness, such as associating partners with Allah and other things. It is permissible that the intended meaning of "people" in the first instance is everyone capable of drowsiness, which is everyone who has come into existence, and in the second instance it refers to jinn and mankind. And Allah knows best.

(p-102)

Ever since the proof of the two horizons and the proof of the two alternating phenomena (the night and the day) established, beyond any doubt, the all-encompassing nature of power together with choice, He said, magnifying Himself with the particle of distance and the mim of plurality: ﴿That is﴾ [i.e.] O you who are addressed! The One, the Subduer, the Mighty in rank, who, through the actions mentioned, has known that none shares with Him, ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., the Greatest King, known to everyone, distinguished from everything by actions in which no one shares with Him. For this reason He said: ﴿your Lord﴾, i.e., the Nurturer of you and the Benefactor to you by His power and choice, the One alone in His lordship over you; there is no lord for you besides Him. And since this was in the context of bestowing blessings, to indicate the Hour which they deny and dispute about, He placed the creation before the declaration of His oneness, saying: ﴿the Creator of all things﴾, i.e., by what has been established of His perfect power in originating the two horizons returning and the two alternating phenomena succeeding one another continuously, and there is no obstacle for Him to restore the two weighty ones (humans and jinn), for He is "there is no god but Allah." Rather, that was necessary in wisdom, because those upon whom He bestowed blessings have divided into the grateful and the disbelievers, so it was necessary in wisdom to establish the Hour to judge between them. This came in the order of the opening of the surah, for the Almighty looks to the perfection of power over origination and annihilation, and the All-Knowing is the One unified in the perfection of His essence, for the comprehensiveness of knowledge entails every perfection, whereas power may not entail knowledge, as with dumb animals. This is unlike what preceded in the verse of al-An'am, for the context there was to deny association and affirm oneness by what indicates it from the generality of creation, in accordance with what also preceded at its opening.

When these statements, each of which confirms what precedes it by being like its cause, produced absolute oneness, from which every perfection necessarily follows, He stated, as a consequence of them, denouncing and rebuking: ﴿So how﴾, i.e., how and from what direction ﴿are you turned away﴾, i.e., you are turned from the faces of the proofs to their backs, so you worship idols and dispute about the Hour, whose denial entails denying wisdom, whose denial entails denying divinity, whose denial entails denying the existence of this existence, and obstinacy in it. That leads to the downfall of the one who speaks it in every respect, because of his obstinacy against what is witnessed and perceived, and against what is innately fixed in all souls.

Once this context revealed that this turning away is something no sensible person would undertake, it was as if it were said: "Has anyone other than these people experienced the like of this?" So He answered with His words: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like this strange turning away, far removed from the ways of the sensible, ﴿are they turned away﴾, that is, they are turned away in an evil turning. He made the verb passive (buniya li-l-maf'ul) to indicate the completeness of His power over it by every means, and also because it is the object of wonder. ﴿Those who used to﴾ be stamped (matbu'in) upon, that they ﴿deny the signs of Allah﴾, that is, of the Lord of Majesty and Beauty, ﴿they deny﴾, that is, they reject out of obstinacy and arrogance. This indicates that everyone who is arrogant toward the truth and rejects it while knowing it is punished by having his heart made dull and his understanding reversed, so that turning away from the faces of the proofs to their backs becomes his habit, to the point that he dies a disbeliever unless Allah overtakes him with mercy from Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 40, verse 64:

Since it has been established that He, glory be to Him, is our Lord alone, and that whoever claims lordship for anything other than Him is an obstinate denier, because He, glory be to Him, is distinguished by His acts, in which none shares with Him, He indicated this by a means fixed in human nature, whose soundness is evident and whose knowledge is clear to the intellects. It is as if he were explaining why this rejection is called *juhud* (denial, obstinate repudiation). So He said, indicating the two horizons (*al-khafiqayn*) after the indication by what arises from them of the *malawayn* (the two alternating phenomena), and He postponed this because, although it is more manifest as a sign of the earth's being a resting place and the sky's being a rotating sphere, the alternation that occurs in them makes this so. He said: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who has complete encompassing knowledge of everything, ﴿who made﴾, that is, alone, ﴿for you the earth﴾, that is, while it is a spread-out bed, ﴿a resting place﴾, while it is in (p-105) the utmost heaviness, and nothing holds it up except His power; ﴿and the sky﴾, despite its height and vastness, while it consists of rotating spheres with stars moving through them over long periods of time, from which arise the night and the day, the darkness and the light, ﴿as a canopy﴾, a covering like a dome, without any supporting pillar. It is known to everyone of understanding that heavy bodies by their nature tend to press down upon one another, so that one body does not prevent another from falling upon it except by force and compulsion. So the verse is an example of *ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which each of two complementary elements is mentioned and the other is left implicit): mentioning "resting place" first indicates "rotation" second, and mentioning "canopy" second indicates "bed" first.

When He mentioned the dwelling, He mentioned the dweller, indicating that He is the one who acts in everything by His choice and His complete power, by fashioning man in a form that no form of any of the animals resembles. He varied among individuals in the shape of that form in ways that can hardly be restricted in themselves, and no one of them resembles another, and there is nothing in the two horizons that resembles them, so that fashioning them upon it is impossible. So He said: ﴿and fashioned you﴾. Fashioning according to no single pattern can only come from the power of a capable agent, complete in power and choosing, not as the people of natures (*ahl al-tabai'*) say.

﴿and made your forms excellent﴾, in shapes and conditions, although they are the most excellent of forms, and there is nothing in existence that resembles them, and there is no form among them that resembles another, so that you could attribute the impression of their fashioning to something else. Thus it is established with certainty that He, glory be to Him, is the Fashioner, without any model, just as He is the One who originated all existence.

When He mentioned the dwelling and the dweller, He mentioned what they need during the period of residence (p-106). He said: ﴿and provided you with good things﴾, the desirable ones that suit natures and are beneficial, in a manner that leaves no need in any respect. There is no clearer proof of complete knowledge, comprehensive power, and the existence of choice than this management: in preserving the dwelling and the roof, and managing what sustains life in a way that suffices the dweller in every respect through the years and the passing of ages. And He spread from the dweller, though it is a very small piece of the surface of the earth, offspring that He divided into tribes, which branched into branches that the earth cannot contain. So with His wisdom, breadth of knowledge and power, He managed a management by which the earth became wide enough for them and provision reached them all. This is as Imam [Ahmad] reported in *al-Zuhd* from al-Hasan, who said: "When Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, and his offspring, the angels, peace be upon them, said: 'Surely the earth cannot contain them.' He said: 'Then I will make death.' They said: 'Then life will not be pleasant for them.' He said: 'Then I will make hope.'"

Since this established with certainty the sole oneness of God, He said, in the form of a conclusion: ﴿That is﴾, that is, the One of exalted ranks, ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Owner of all dominion, [and He guided them to what has passed through their upbringing and the marvelous crafts within it, so He said]: ﴿your Lord﴾, [that is]: none other than Him. Since this proof conveys a nurture without equal, indicating the comprehensiveness of knowledge and the completeness of power, for it is in a manner that needs nothing beyond it, along with its goodness and stability (p-107), His statement must necessarily follow: ﴿So blessed be﴾, that is, He is established in a great stability, together with abundance, goodness, and the excellence of aid and overflowing bounty, ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One specially characterized by perfection. [And the address rose and became greater in clarifying the proof, so He said]: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, all of them, you and others. Then He indicated what the proof conveys, giving the reason in His saying:

﴿He﴾, that is, He alone is ﴿the Ever-Living﴾. Everything other than Him has no life, because it possesses of its own essence nothing but non-existence. From this there necessarily follows His saying: ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾. Consequent upon it is His saying: ﴿so call upon Him﴾, that is, call upon Him alone, by word and deed, in the manner of worship. This is the meaning of ﴿sincere in devotion to Him, the religion﴾, that is, free from every shirk, whether manifest or hidden.

When He commanded that aspirations be confined to Him, He gave the reason in His saying: ﴿The praise﴾, that is, the comprehensive possession of all attributes of perfection, [and He placed the noun in the position of the pronoun (iḍmār), indicating that He has of the supreme attributes what cannot be counted]: ﴿belongs to Allah﴾, that is, to the One named by this name, which by His essence comprises all the meanings of the Most Beautiful Names. Since this existence, in the state of order and wondrous arrangement in which it is, indicates the praise with a definitive indication, He described Him, with a description that serves as the cause of knowledge of the content of the report, saying: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, that is, the One who nurtured them with this nurturing, for it could not be otherwise.

On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both (p-108), he said: "Whoever says (There is no deity but Allah), let him say immediately after it (All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds)."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 40, verse 66:

When Allah, glorified is He, commanded what indicates that He alone deserves worship, He necessarily produced His saying: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to those who dispute with you about monotheism and the resurrection, responding to their denial with emphasis: ﴿Indeed, I have been forbidden﴾, that is, by the One besides whom there is no one who forbids, a general prohibition established by the proofs of reason and a specific prohibition established by the evidences of transmitted texts, ﴿to worship﴾. And since they had raised these [deities] to the highest ranks, He referred to them, leaving the reins loose, by His saying: ﴿those whom you invoke﴾, that is, those who qualify them to be invoked by you. He indicated their lowliness by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿besides Allah﴾, [that is]: the One who possesses all perfection. And He indicated that he was not a worshipper under the law (shar') of any prophet before the mission by His saying: ﴿since there have come to me the clear proofs﴾, that is, the evident arguments, very manifest, from the proofs of reason and of transmission. [And He turned the speech to the attribute of benevolence, as an alert that just as He deserves to be singled out in worship for His own essence, He also deserves it in gratitude for His benevolence, so He said]: ﴿from my Lord﴾, that is, the One who nurtures me with a special nurturing that is higher than the nurturing of every creature other than me; therefore I worship Him with a worship that surpasses the worship of every worshipper.

When He informed [him] of what he disassociates himself from, He followed it with the command to what he adorns himself with, and said: ﴿And I have been commanded to submit﴾, that is, that I renew the submission of my whole being at [every] (p-109) time, continuously, ﴿to the Lord of the worlds﴾, because everything other than Him is a thing nurtured, so turning toward it is loss. And since he, (ﷺ), was forbidden from that and commanded with this, because the one who commands and the one who forbids is his Lord, who is the Lord of everything, then others necessarily share with him in that.

Now for the translation.

When the proofs were established and the arguments shone forth that He, glory be to Him, is the Lord of the worlds, of whom the addressees are a part, and that nature has no command, nor anything else, He followed this with another sign within themselves, which is clearer than what preceded it. So he connected it, by way of causation, to the previous verse because they share with him ﷺ in the matter of commanding and forbidding. This is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿He is the One﴾, not other than Him, ﴿who﴾ (ﷺ) — and since the attribute of nurturing was past, he expressed it with it, saying: ﴿created you from dust﴾, that is, your origin and your food by which your bodies are nurtured; ﴿then from a drop﴾ of semen that is emitted; ﴿then from a clinging clot﴾, distancing its state from the state of the drop just as the state of the drop was distant from the state of dust.

﴿Then﴾, after other conditions had passed, ﴿He brings you forth﴾, that is, He renews your bringing forth, one thing after another, ﴿as infants﴾, who own nothing and know nothing. Then He leads you through the stages of nurture, ascending in strength to the peak of perfection, stage after stage and state after state, ﴿that you may reach your maturity, then﴾ He lowers you through weakness and feebleness into the pits of decline, ﴿that you may become elders﴾, weak and strangers, whose peers have died and whose pillars have grown feeble, so that you fear everyone.

Since this implied that it is the condition of everyone, He clarified that only some are intended by it, because the addressee is the species, which encompasses some as it encompasses all. So He said: ﴿And among you is one who is taken in death﴾, by the seizing of his soul and all its meanings.

Since death does not occupy the whole time that lies between the ages, but is in a brief moment within them, he introduced the preposition before the adverbial noun, saying: ﴿before﴾, that is, before the state of old age or before the state of maturity.

Since the meaning is that your lifespans, conditions and deeds may differ, He joined to it His saying: ﴿and that you may reach﴾, that is, each one of you, ﴿an appointed term﴾, that is, [for him] which the Angel appointed over him in his mother's womb by Our permission and command, which We have decreed from eternity, so that it is never exceeded, nor by the weight of an atom, lest faith be renewed for the angels at every time.

Since these matters are certain for those who know them, and unattainable for those who are ignorant of them, and since no human can reach any of them by stratagem or thought, He expressed them with the lām. Reflection and contemplation upon them, leading to knowledge that God is One, is a hope for the intelligent, so He said: ﴿so that perhaps you will understand﴾, [that is]: that you may know, through the variation among people in these matters, by demonstrative proofs, by turning over the stages of creation and the periods of ages, and by referring the final judgments back to the first, that the Doer of this is All-Powerful, Chooser, Wise, Subduing, resembling nothing, and nothing resembles Him.

When He (glory be to Him) had arranged this proof regarding the creation of man from dust, and concluded it by showing that its indication of resurrection, by the operation of His custom of returning the last of matters to their first, and other things, requires nothing beyond reason, He produced from it [this statement]: ﴿He is the One who gives life and causes death﴾, not any other, as you observe in yourselves, and as the indication of this was previously made to you by the creation of the heavens and the earth. For whoever created them created what is between them, including the appointed terms that are set by the alternation of night and day, the months and the years, so that the spheres reach their places, and then their return, repeating the beginning, like the development of man after being dust, from a drop of semen to a clinging clot and beyond it, and then his return, in the stages of his descent, until he becomes dust as he was. So the end is not more remote than the beginning.

Since His will is only ever complete and effective, He based on this His saying, expressing it with the word "decree": ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾, that is, wills any matter whatsoever, whether of the Resurrection or other than it, ﴿He only says to it, "Be," and it is﴾. Since "when" (idhā) is a conditional particle, [Ibn ʿĀmir] answered it in his recitation with His saying ﴿and it is﴾ (fa-yakūnu). In the recitation of others, he conjoined it to "Be" (kun) in view of its meaning, or it is a predicate of an implied subject [i.e.]: "so He is one who causes it to be." He used the present tense to depict the state and to inform of its renewal at every decree. The full discussion of the justification of Ibn ʿĀmir's recitation (qirāʾa) has already been given in Sūrat al-Baqara, by which it became clear that it is (p-١١٢) stronger than the recitation of others.

When He knew from this that for Him there is no burden in any of these matters, which are witnessed in their own selves and in the horizons, He produced wonder at their condition for the one who has piercing understanding and blazing insight, and He made that among His dazzling signs and His manifest overpowering might. Therefore He said, turning the address to the highest of creation, because censure of disputing in falsehood is the purpose of this surah:

﴿Have you not seen﴾ That is: O brightest of people in heart and purest of them in intellect. He then specified them after him with the particle of ultimacy, saying: ﴿those who dispute﴾ That is: in falsehood. And He drew attention, through repeating the all-encompassing Name, to the greatness in these verses that has no end, saying: ﴿in the signs of Allah﴾ That is: the King [the Supreme].

﴿How﴾ That is: and how, and from what direction, ﴿are they turned away﴾ from the true and clear signs that have preceded, by primordial nature, to the roots of their hearts. So they bring no proof, and they find no escape from punishment for themselves. For He, glorified is He, has driven them, as Ibn Burjan said, with the chains of His overpowering, forged from the pure resolves and endurances of their wills, from the reality of their very selves, toward the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. He then detailed what they disputed about, describing them in a way that increases the wonder at the intensity of their ignorance and the magnitude of their blindness, saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 70:

﴿Those who denied﴾: the object is omitted to indicate the generality of the denial. ﴿The Book﴾, that is, they denied it in respect of all of its affairs, which are beyond enumeration and of great magnitude, in every matter. [As] the particle of perfection indicates, its perfection is such that it is as though there were no other book, because whoever hears it is as though he heard it from the Prophet (ﷺ), by virtue of its inimitability (i'jaz, the miraculous quality that renders it unmatched). Thus whoever denies a single letter of it has denied all of Allah's Book.

Since denying it amounts to denying all the divine messages, He affirmed its greatness by this and by its attribution to the source of greatness, as a warning to the deniers of His punishment and a reminder to them that acting against the Messenger is acting against the One who sent him. Therefore the speech turns to the Name that combines the attributes of majesty and generosity (al-Jalal wa'l-Ikram), and He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And with that with which We sent﴾, that is, in accordance with the greatness We possess, ﴿Our messengers﴾ from all the religious communities (milal) and laws (shara'i'), whether with a Book or without one. It is of such a nature that its reality cannot be encompassed, nor the greatness of its state. For this reason, a threat against them is consequent upon it in His words, exalted is He: ﴿They will come to know﴾, that is, through a truthful promise in which there is no breach, what will befall them of Our punishment.

When they were in this world, their hands were gathered to their chins by the bonds of subjugation, and then they were joined with chains of compulsion, by which they are driven away from the station of success and triumph into the abysses of disbelief, through disputation with falsehood and through the wastelands of manifest error. This is as the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We have put shackles upon their necks, up to the chins, so they are held erect﴾ [Ya-Sin: 8], and so He made the inner reality of those worldly chains and shackles apparent in that gathering. He said: ﴿When﴾, meaning: at the time when ﴿the shackles﴾ are present, plural of ghull (shackle). In Diwan al-Adab (Diwan al-Adab, a lexicon), it is said that it is that by which a person is punished. Al-Qazzaz said: the ghull made of iron is well known, and it may be made of rawhide. In al-Nihaya (al-Nihaya, the lexicon of Ibn al-Athir) it is said: it is the iron ring that gathers the captive's hand to his neck, and it is also called jami'a. End of quotation. Its origin is insertion: the neck and the hand enter into it and are thereby bound together. This is the meaning of the words of al-Saghani in Majma' al-Bahrayn (Majma' al-Bahrayn, by al-Saghani): "On his neck is a ghull of iron, and his hand has been shackled to his neck." ﴿in their necks﴾, meaning: gathering their hands to their collarbones. He used ﴿when﴾, which means the past, together with ﴿soon﴾, which means the future, because expressing it in the past tense indicates the certainty of the matter even though it is yet to come.

﴿And the chains﴾, meaning: also in their necks, by which that restrains them from every free action, because they were not bound by a Book or a Messenger. The word silsila (chain) derives from tasalsala al-shay', meaning it became disturbed. Al-Raghib said: it is as if a continuous, recurring motion was imagined from it, so its word was repeated to indicate the recurrence of its meaning, and "masalsal" is that which recurs in its place until it becomes clear. The state of their being ﴿dragged﴾, meaning: by them, and al-sahb is pulling by force.

in the scalding water. That is, the hot water that is present, which brings blackness to faces, shame to honor, torment to spirits, fire to bodies, distress to hearts, and melting and wasting to flesh. This is the recompense for their elevating themselves above dragging themselves through the causes of clear proofs, through the burdens of worship, the bitterness of striving, and the heats of the trials they encountered.

When he had informed of their being tormented with scalding water, which by its nature constricts the breaths, weakens the powers, and softens the hearts, he informed of what is beyond that, saying: ﴿Then in the Fire﴾, that is, its torment specifically, ﴿they are kindled﴾, that is, they are cast into it and it is fired up with them piled up, bound together, just as the oven (tannur) is kindled with firewood, meaning it is filled, and its fire blazes; and just as the water is poured (yusjaru, "is poured") into the throat, so they fill it and it is thereby heated and its blazing intensifies, because while they were in the world they were fuel for sins, and through them the fuel of trials ignites, its firewood grows strong, and its pillar becomes firm, because they did not cast themselves into the fires of enjoining good and forbidding evil, and opposing the desires in the matters of commands and prohibitions, which are in outward appearance fires, but in reality gardens.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 73:

Since the one who is called upon is only stored up for times of hardship, He said, rebuking them, shaming them, and denouncing the shortness of their view of themselves, using the passive form because the one who would deliver this statement is absolute, not because it comes from a specific speaker: ﴿Then it will be said to them﴾, that is, after their punishment had lengthened and reached them in every degree, and they found no helper to rescue them nor an intercessor to aid them: ﴿Where﴾. The expression by the interrogative particle used for those who do not reason is in its most judicious place in His saying: ﴿what you used to be﴾, that is, constantly, ﴿associating (with Allah)﴾, that is, by calling upon those (false gods) for your needs in the manner of worship, renewing this at every time;

Then He explained their abasement by His words, turning the speech from the manifestation of greatness to something greater than it, so He said: ﴿besides Allah﴾, meaning the One who encompasses all might and all greatness, so that you would seek from them your rescue from what you are in, or its lightening. ﴿They will say﴾, meaning, going along with the innate nature, which is the first nature upon truthfulness: ﴿They have strayed from us﴾, so we do not see them, just as we strayed in the world from what would benefit us.

When they saw that their truthfulness had obliged them to acknowledge their shirk, the vileness of deception and the baseness of their characters led them to lying. They went along with it and hastened to show harshness, saying, disguising themselves before the One who knows the treachery of eyes and what the breasts conceal, thinking that this would benefit them as it used to benefit them among the believers in the abode of the world: ﴿Rather, we were not calling﴾, meaning, that was not in our nature. Since their intent was to negate their calling upon anything at all, fundamentally and entirely, for a moment or more, and not a restricted negation limited to the totality, for that does not negate what is less than it, they affirmed the adverbial phrase, so they said: ﴿before﴾, meaning before this (p-117) return, ﴿anything﴾, so that we would have been associating with Him. Thus Allah would not empower them except for what increases their harm, doubles their regret, and makes them [curse] themselves and curse one another [each other], such that they would not cease to be in regret, as was their state in the world. ﴿Look how they lied against themselves, and what they used to fabricate has strayed from them﴾ [al-An'am: 24]. So the verse is of ihtibak: mentioning the shirk first is evidence of their negation of it second, and the calling second is evidence of its estimation first.

Since this was at the utmost of wonder regarding their misguidance, it was as if it were said: Does any of creation go astray with the straying of these people? So it was answered with His words: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning, yes, like this far-removed straying from the right course, ﴿Allah leads astray﴾, meaning, the One who encompasses all in knowledge and power, from the beneficial aim, of proof and other than it, ﴿the disbelievers﴾, meaning, those who concealed the mirrors of their insights so that it would not be displayed in them, and then that became their habit.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 75:

When the answer to the question about the wonder at this misguidance was complete, he returned to addressing the misguided, saying, magnifying what he had mentioned of their recompense by the particle of distance and the plural mim, explicitly as a rebuke to each one of them: ﴿That is for you﴾, i.e., the recompense, great in its ranks, [arduous] in its vehicles, mighty in its processions, ﴿because you used to﴾, i.e., constantly, ﴿exult﴾, i.e., you exceed the bounds in joy, immerse yourselves in it, and are too weak to bear it, due to turning away from the consequences. Since the earth was a prison, [it is] in reality (p-118) the abode of sorrows, his saying is fine: ﴿in the earth﴾, i.e., so you acted in it contrary to what I had set it up for. What added to this fineness is his saying ﴿without right﴾, which indicates that joy is not fitting except when it is accompanied by the perfection of this reality, namely permanence forever for that in which one rejoices, and that does not occur except in Paradise. ﴿And because﴾, i.e., and by reason of what, ﴿you used to be insolent﴾, i.e., you exceed the bounds in exultation together with the worst of conditions, arrogance, insolence, and the vigor that necessitates vanity, strutting, and lightness, through being unable to bear the joy.

When the context is the condemnation of disputation, and disputation arises only from arrogance, and joy is not necessarily tied to arrogance, the entry into the Fire was not attributed to it as its cause. Rather, He made it like the result of everything that preceded, so He said: ﴿Enter﴾, meaning: O you who denied.

Since the Fire contains various kinds of punishment, He indicated that they would be punished with each kind by mentioning the gates, as a recompense for their plunging, through their disputation, into every kind of falsehood. So He said: ﴿the gates of Hell﴾, [meaning] the stratum (al-darkah) that casts its occupant with arrogance, sullenness and scowling, ﴿abiding therein﴾, meaning: remaining in what you began by entering, a remaining from which there is no escape at all.

Since it was an extreme in ugliness, disgrace and evil, and since their entry into it, coupled with their eternal abiding, was a cause for something like the saying "So it is your abode," He made His statement ﴿how wretched is the abode﴾ a consequence of this, rather than saying "the entrance of ﴿the arrogant﴾", meaning: the place of (p-119) their residence, judged to be necessary for them because they took up what was not theirs, when it should belong to none but Allah. Allah the Exalted says: "Greatness is My cloak and majesty is My waistwrap; whoever disputes with Me over either of them, I shatter him." He did not emphasize the clause "how wretched" here, because their argument [in the Hereafter] is built upon their renewed knowledge of the states of the Fire and of what caused it. Emphasis is used for one who denies, and those like him, and the state of each of these two contradicts knowledge. What made this even better is that the original speech was addressed to one who knows the secret that has preceded, so emphasis would be far out of place.

When this was the greatest gloating over them in the requital, and it was for those who disputed with him and were arrogant toward him the greatest consolation, he made it a consequence of that, saying: ﴿So be patient﴾ [i.e.], awaiting this victory. Then he gave the reason, emphatically, to counter their denial of the promise, with his saying: ﴿Indeed the promise of God﴾, i.e., the One combining all the attributes of perfection, ﴿is true﴾, i.e., regarding your victory in both abodes, so it must come to pass. In this is the greatest consolation for you. For this reason he made it a consequence, while diverting the speech to what follows of the *i'tirāḍ* (parenthetical interjection), as an indication that He is not questioned about what He does. His exalted saying: ﴿So whether We show you﴾ is emphasized with *mā* and the *nūn*. The manifestation of greatness here is due to their denial of His victory over them and of their being raised again: ﴿some of what We promise them﴾, i.e., with what We possess of greatness, of what would gladden you regarding them, of punishment or of return (*matāb*) before your death. That is up to Us, and it is easy for Us.

When he mentioned the conditional verb and omitted its answer because it was known, he joined to it his saying (p-120): ﴿or We cause you to die﴾ [i.e.], before you see that happen to them. This conjoined clause is answered by his saying: ﴿then to Us they will be returned﴾, i.e., by what We possess of greatness, [meaning] in this world, so We show them after your death who helped your companions against them, with what gladdens you in your *barzakh* (intermediate state), for there is no permanence to the rounds of their falsehood; and in the Resurrection, in actuality, so We show you concerning them more than you hope for of victory, which includes your being affirmed and their being denied, and your honor and their humiliation. The verse is of *ihtibāk* (a rhetorical device in which one element is omitted from each of two parallel parts, each omission being indicated by the other): he mentioned the death second as an indication of its omission first, and the seeing first as an indication of its omission second.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 78:

When Allah, glorified is He, divided the matter for him (ﷺ) between their being struck (by punishment) or his death (ﷺ), and there remained, of what is more pleasing to his eye and more soothing to his chest, that He show them in his lifetime a sign that compels them to faith and brings them to agreement and submission, so that dispute ends through good following, as happened to the people of Yunus, upon him be peace, He said, linking it to what is implied in the reason for the command to patience: "Indeed We have sent you to them, and We will surely carry out Our command concerning them, while as for you, your duty is only to convey (the message)": ﴿And We have certainly sent messengers﴾, i.e., with what We possess of greatness, ﴿messengers﴾, i.e., in great number.

Since sending (of messengers) is only in some part of past time, although the delivery of each messenger's message to those who come after him necessitates that the ruling of his message extends until the coming of the messenger who follows him, He affirmed the preposition to indicate the reality, and said: ﴿from before you﴾, i.e., to their nations, so that they might convey from Us what We commanded them with. (p-121) ﴿Of them are those We have related﴾, i.e., by what We possess of comprehensiveness, ﴿to you﴾, i.e., the accounts of them and the accounts of their nations; ﴿and of them are those We have not related﴾, although We have complete knowledge and perfect power, ﴿to you﴾, neither their accounts nor the accounts of their nations, nor have We mentioned them to you by their names. ﴿And it was not for any messenger﴾, i.e., We sent them while the state was that it was not at all ﴿for a messenger﴾ ﴿to bring a sign﴾, i.e., one compelling or not compelling, of what the messenger seeks in haste for his people to follow him, or by suggestion from his people to him, or otherwise, of what he disputes with his people or what they submit to him or comply with; and He turned the speech away from the manifestation pointing to compulsion to what contains, along with humiliation, honor, so He said: ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by His command and enablement, for He has comprehension of everything, so nothing goes out of His command. If He does not permit it, they are content, submit, are patient, and are restrained; and if He permits any of that, a punishment or a compelling sign or otherwise, what He permitted comes to them. ﴿So when there comes﴾ — and the matter increases in magnitude for the greater fear and hope by the explicit mention rather than by pronoun — He said: ﴿the command of Allah﴾, i.e., He who encompasses everything in power and knowledge; and His command is what He threatened of punishment upon obstinacy after granting the suggested (sign), and of the Resurrection and what is in it. The repetition of the Greatest Name is to magnify the station by bringing to mind what He has of attributes of majesty and generosity; and for the firmness and permanence of what He willed, He expressed it by "decree" (qadaa'), so He said, indicating the form of the passive with utmost ease: ﴿it is decreed﴾, i.e., by His command in the easiest and most facile manner, ﴿with truth﴾, i.e., the established matter that was previously promised and whose establishment He decreed: the destruction of some people and the salvation of others, or the faith of a people and the disbelief of others. All of this is what Allah, glorified is He, has made His ancient practice to take effect by its establishment; as for the bounty of respite and the favor of blessings, it is only before granting the suggested things. The evidence that this is among the intended meanings of the verse is what comes after it in His saying: ﴿So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might﴾ [Ghafir: 85], and what resembles it. ﴿And there lose﴾, i.e., perish, or it is confirmed and made clear by witnessing that they lost ﴿there﴾, i.e., at that momentous time with the greatness of what We sent down in it — an adverbial of place used for time, as a notification of the utmost firmness and settledness in loss, like the settledness of one who sits; ﴿the falsifiers﴾, i.e., those ascribed to preferring falsehood over truth, either by suggesting signs while having what suffices them without them and calling it sorcery, or otherwise; either by being easily able to return from what they are in of obstinacy without submission, or destruction; or by refuting proofs and judging against them with defeat and then the Fire, even if after a while. From this verse Allah, glorified is He, began to answer the conclusion of the surah with its opening. So this verse looks to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And every nation schemed against their messenger to seize him﴾ [Ghafir: 5], [﴿And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign﴾] up to ﴿and they argued with falsehood﴾ [Ghafir: 5], (p-123) and ﴿Have they not traveled in the land﴾ [Ghafir: 82] up to ﴿so I seized them, and how was My punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 5]. This and what follows it, of what it contains of wisdom and power, extends to the first three verses.

Since the wrongdoers (al-mubtiluun) are no more averse to the truth, nor stronger, than some of the dumb animals, He indicated, through what He informed of His effective victory over them, by His saying, reminding them of His favor, inviting them to obedience, and pointing to tawhid (affirming God's oneness) after softening them with the threat. He manifested the all-comprehensive Name (al-ism al-jami') to show that this verse is among the indications that cannot be counted: ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the Greatest King, ﴿who made for you﴾, and no other than Him, ﴿the cattle﴾, that is, the eight pairs, by subjugation and making them subservient, ﴿that you may ride of them﴾. These are the camels, with their strength and their aversion. The expression with the preposition "li-" (for/in order that) applied to riding is unrestricted, and then it is restricted to reaching distant places. This indicates that this is the purpose intended from them in essence, and it is what necessitated their being composed as they are. From it there arose the remaining benefits, which were therefore secondary.

Since eating from them, in its great benefit, abundance, and desirability, is such that nothing else is comparable to it, He counted the others as non-existent. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿of them﴾, that is, of all the cattle, ﴿you eat﴾. The prepositional phrase ("of them") is placed first (bi-taqdim al-jarr), which is the grammatical device of fronting the prepositional phrase for emphasis and restriction.

When the disposal of them was not confined to a fixed scope, he summarized it with His words: ﴿And for you in them﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿there are benefits﴾, that is, many benefits besides that, in their milk, their wool, their fleece and other things.

When their driving, and reaching remote places on them in the shortest time, was for obtaining great and momentous matters of very great benefit, he drew attention to its greatness by moving from the general mention of benefits to a detailed account of them, saying: ﴿and that you may reach﴾, that is, rising high ﴿upon them﴾, while they are in the utmost submission and obedience, and he alerted them to their own deficiency and to the great favor of His bestowal upon them by His words: ﴿a need﴾, that is, he made it generic, the need.

Since this was a context of magnifying His blessings, for it belongs to the setting of bestowing favor and showing power alone, and gathering what is concealed in it, he said: ﴿in your breasts﴾, indicating that a single need was too much for the hearts of all of them, until it overflowed from them and filled their dwellings.

Since carrying occurs with any kind of elevation, whether it is on the top of a thing or not, unlike riding, he used the particle of elevation for it and for the ship, other than the ship of Noah, peace be upon him, for it was covered, as is related, so they were within its belly [not] on its back, saying: ﴿and upon them﴾, that is, on land, ﴿and upon the ship﴾, that is, at sea, ﴿you are carried﴾, that is, it carries your goods for you, for a person's carrying of himself was already mentioned through riding.

By using the passive form of the verb, he indicated that He subjected these to your service with a great subjection, such that no treatment is needed with it in the act of carrying itself.

Since this is a great sign, He (glory be to Him) made it comprise many signs. He expressed it in the past tense and conjoined it with the present tense, to draw attention to renewal, with the implied sense: "So He shows you these clear signs from among them." His saying ﴿And He shows you﴾, i.e., in a single moment, ﴿His signs﴾, i.e., the many and great ones in them and in others, from your own selves and from the horizons. The omission of the feminine ta' (in ﴿āyāt﴾, the plural form) indicates the abundance and greatness of the signs, as is well known in other than the vocative, through the explicit mention of the Greatest Name in His saying: ﴿So which of the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., of the One encompassing all the attributes of perfection, ﴿will you deny?﴾, until the dispute about His signs, of which the clearest is the Resurrection, is directed at you.

Then, when the matter had reached a degree of clarity that no one could fail to see, the address was turned away from them, as a sign of the anger that calls for punishment and demands awe. So He said: ﴿Have they not traveled in the earth﴾ [i.e., these people, who are more astray than cattle] ﴿in the earth﴾, whatever land it might be, traveling with the traveling of reflection (i'tibar) ﴿and seen﴾ with the seeing of remembrance (idkar) into what happened to its inhabitants and its regions. He alerted to the increased greatness in what He urged them to look into, by putting it in the form of a question, to draw attention to its being unlike its like and set apart from its kind, through His saying: ﴿how was the end﴾, i.e., the final outcome ﴿of those who﴾. Since they were not able to comprehend the sight of the whole earth and the traces of all its people, He alerted by the preposition [to] what is within reach, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿before them﴾, i.e., despite the nearness of time and place, although they relied on overpowering the Messenger ﷺ and disputing with him in falsehood, despite the clear signs, in spite of their numbers and strength and the fewness of his companions along with their weakness. The denunciation of them had already been made in the dispute, to refute the truth, and their great rebuke for not looking, while traveling the earth, with eyes of reflection upon the remains, from the dwellings and abodes, of those among the wicked who passed away. He affirmed for them superiority, and that it did not avail them. He mentioned Pharaoh and what he had of power through wealth and men, and that He seized him with a seizing that became a proverb among proverbs. There remained, of what they might cite in their overpowering, numbers; He mentioned it joined to strength, as confirmation of the content of the report, that no command of anyone stands against His command. So He said, starting a new sentence as an answer to one who asks: What was their end? He said: ﴿They were more numerous than them﴾, i.e., in number, many times over, [and] especially the people of Noah, peace be upon him, ﴿and greater in strength﴾ in bodies, like the people of Hud, peace be upon him, who said, as will come in the following verse: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat: 15] ﴿and in traces in the earth﴾, by hewing houses out of the mountains, digging wells, channeling waters, building great reservoirs, and other things that they used to do.

Since the implied sense is: so they looked, and then Allah destroyed them, He made their greater numbers and their strength in power the cause of His saying, as an explicit negation or as a denying interrogative: ﴿So what availed them﴾, i.e., what thing or what wealth ﴿did not avail them of anything of wealth, [of] what they used to earn﴾, i.e., constantly, as is natural to them from their motives, ﴿by the strength of their bodies, the greatness of their minds, their cunning, and the reservoirs they built for their deliverance, when Our command came upon them. Rather, they were like yesterday that has passed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 83:

When He informed of their multitude, their strength, and their monuments that indicate their power [mukna], He then followed this with an explanation of their condition, which led to their destruction and annihilation. He said, clarifying what had been left vague: ﴿When their messengers came to them﴾, that is, those whom We sent to them and who were from among them, whose truthfulness and trustworthiness they knew, ﴿with the clear proofs﴾, that is, the proofs that indicate their truthfulness beyond doubt. ﴿They rejoiced﴾, that is, the people described ﴿in what knowledge they had﴾, the knowledge by which they left those traces on the earth: the extraction of water, the moving of heavy loads, the planning of buildings, knowledge of the climes, and the observation of the stars to learn the conditions of livelihood, and other outward sciences that led to boasting, self-magnification, and rivalry in accumulation, standing still with illusion and restricting themselves to what is present of the outward form, the knowledge of the outward life of this world, and contentment with what is transient. This is as He said in the verse before it: ﴿Then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I have only been given it on knowledge"﴾ [az-Zumar: 49]. And as Qarun said when it was said to him, ﴿And do good as Allah has done good to you﴾ [al-Qasas: 77], he said: ﴿I have only been given it on knowledge that is with me﴾ [al-Qasas: 78]. And it made them rejoice (p-128) because it led them to expansion in this world and to delighting in it. They mocked what the messengers brought them of the knowledge of the inner reality, which calls to turning away from the transient and turning toward the enduring, and to fear of what comes after death of unseen matters, coming terrors, and great events hidden behind the veil of this frail worldly life, with all its essences, meanings, states, fears, and calamities. What moved them to rejoice in what they had was [the fact] that they were in splendor, while they saw the messengers and their followers living in poverty of worldly things, calamities hastening upon them, and the great number of griefs and sorrows they suffered, and the rivals and opponents they endured. So their mockery of them and of what they brought intensified, deeming it all impossible, false, and misguided. They never ceased from the rejoicing that is insolent and exultant, from laughing and swaggering, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when he came to them with Our signs, they laughed at them﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 47]. They set up schemes against the messengers and their followers, surrounded them with deceit and treachery, and resolved to seize them. So We saved Our messengers and those who believed with them, and We gave them what removed their rejoicing and prolonged their grief and distress. ﴿And there befell﴾, that is, there encompassed, in the manner of severity, ﴿them what they used to﴾, that is, a continuous habit.

Since their mockery of the truth was exceedingly great, he counted their mockery of anything else as nothing, and indicated this by placing the circumstantial phrase first, saying: ﴿at it they mock﴾, referring to the threat (p-129) which they were certain was false. Thus it is known with certainty that they rejoice only in knowledge that contains salvation and eternal happiness. Moreover, the flow of this discourse is full of mockery of them and scorn at them, because they set up the eloquent debater [al-mantiq], who, when he overcomes his opponent, silences him, makes him bite the stone, renders him mute and tongue-tied with clear proof and straight path, shows joy and is overcome by gladness. But if his opponent persists and stands by his illusion, he mocks him and laughs at him. This is in addition to what they have of the blindnesses of ignorance, which they cannot deny, as shown by the acknowledgment of those to whom this noble Prophet was sent that the People of the Book are more knowledgeable than they. So they would direct their mounts to the Jews, asking them about [their affair], while his affair [is that] he has come to them with what elevates their rank over the People of the Book and makes them those singled out for lordship over the passing ages. Yet they refuse, in their disputation with falsehood, anything but baseness, turning away from what is right, deviating, recoiling, and refusing. The verse also guides to the fact that no one learns except one who regards himself as deficient, and for this reason the most receptive thing to knowledge is humility. This verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical figure in which one element is mentioned and its counterpart is omitted, and the omitted counterpart in the second part is indicated by the mention in the first part, and vice versa): mention of rejoicing first indicates the omission of its opposite second, and mention of mockery second indicates the omission of its like first.

Since this surah is concerned with explaining the might (al-'izzah), which is the result of perfect knowledge and comprehensive power, and since the greatness of might is proportionate to the greatness of the one seized by it who opposes it, He repeated the mention of disputation in this surah, a repetition that signaled this. He said at its beginning: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve﴾ [Ghafir: 4]. Then He showed that they are seized without their disputation, which their misguidance produced, being of any benefit to them, and [showed] its consequences, as encouragement and warning, until He said: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs﴾ [Ghafir: 13]. He mentioned some of what had become so familiar to them that its strangeness had fallen away from them, and He drew their attention to what is in it, so that He might restrain them from disputation and make them content with it, and not demand something else. Then He mentioned the story of Musa, peace be upon him, reminding them of what befell the deniers who disputed after the signs they had demanded had come, by their saying: ﴿So bring a sign, if you are of the truthful﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 154]. He continued to remind, warn, and caution in those methods that are sharper than swords and clearer than suns in clear weather, not in eclipse, until He said: ﴿Those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority that has come to them, greatly hateful is it in the sight of Allah and in the sight of those who believe﴾ [Ghafir: 35]. Then He began completing the story of Musa, peace be upon him, until He said: ﴿Indeed, those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah without authority that has come to them—there is nothing in their breasts except pride, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir: 56]. Then He began enumerating the great signs which, because of their extreme clarity, refuse the disputation of the disputer and the misguidance of the obstinate and hostile one, were it not that the intensity of familiarity with them had removed them from the realm of strangeness: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the folding of the night and the day [al-malawayn], the spreading of the earth, the raising of the sky, the forming of man and the great matter within him. So familiarity uncovered their veils and clarified their indication and manifestness. He turned the discourse to a threat against the disputers, saying in rebuke of them: ﴿Have you not seen those who dispute concerning the signs of Allah—how are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 69], in the manner of eloquent speakers: when one silences his opponent with something from his own proofs, as clear as the sun in light, radiance, and manifestness, he rebukes him with a question, which is like the striking of arrows.

When their obstinacy, harshness, and strength in their stubbornness and vehemence were thereby established, He explained their ignorance through their humbling of themselves when the consequences of their affair appeared to them, and when the heavy burdens of punishment that exceed their powers were about to descend upon them. So there was undone what they had firmly knotted of their evil. He said, explaining what had been left general about the calamity and making it a consequence of it, turning the speech to the manifestation of majesty as an instilling of awe: ﴿So when they saw Our might﴾, meaning they witnessed ﴿Our might﴾, i.e., Our severe punishment, with the majesty by which its attribution to Us and its issuing from Us is exalted. ﴿They said, "We believe in Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses the totality of majesty, the bonds of might, and the executing of the command, as has become apparent to us in this might, without ambiguity or confusion. They emphasized this, negating what they had been in [of polytheism] by their saying ﴿alone﴾. It indicated the dissolution of their bonds and the weakening of their strength by the added explicitness in their saying ﴿and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him﴾, i.e., by disposition and nature ﴿as partners﴾, because we knew that nothing beside Allah avails anything.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 40, verse 85:

(p-132) Since disbelief in the unseen is a cause for faith not being accepted at the time of witnessing, He said: ﴿So it was not⦗that⦘﴾, meaning: it was not valid and was not accepted in any way whatsoever, because no existence assists it, nor even the lowest degree of existence. By using "kāna" (was) He indicated that this is a settled matter and a continuous affair for every nation, not specific to those spoken of here and those who passed before them. [And] by omitting the final letter of the word (i.e., the "lām" of the root), He indicated that they went to extremes in weakening faith through its affirmation, its repetition and its clarification, in its release and its dismissal, while the time was narrow and the arena confined, and the Imminent Event (al-Āzifah) had drawn near, "there is none to remove it besides Allah" (53:58). Because the time had passed, they were not fulfilling what was demanded of them. ﴿Their faith did not benefit them﴾, meaning: its benefit does not newly accrue to them after that, because it is the faith of compulsion and necessity, not the faith of willing obedience and choice. ﴿When they saw﴾ [and] he made explicit the position where a pronoun would have been expected, for added warning, so He said: ﴿Our might﴾, because faith is not realized nor conceivable except with the unseen. As for at the time of witnessing, its inner reality has been exposed, and its true nature and form have passed; so even if they were returned, they would revert, and even if the punishment came to them after that, they would submit. For this very secret, the Exalted said, turning the speech to the Name that entails the blending of wisdom with greatness: ﴿The way of Allah﴾, meaning: the Greatest King, encompassing in knowledge and power, established this in every age as a practice (sunnah). Therefore He said: ﴿which has passed among His servants﴾, that faith after the unveiling of the veil is not accepted, and every nation that denied the messengers was destroyed, and everyone who was called to faith in the manner requested and did not believe was punished. He established it as a practice and confirmed it as a firm decree, so there is no alteration to it. ﴿And there the believers won﴾ (p-133) at that time, ﴿and the disbelievers lost﴾, meaning: they perished, or it became established and clear that they had lost. Since place cannot be separated from time, its locative form was borrowed for it, and to indicate the utmost firmness, it was said: ﴿There﴾, meaning: at that momentous time with what it contained. And ﴿the disbelievers﴾ were, meaning: those thoroughly steeped in this description, so there is no separation between them and it. The end of the surah is bound to what was made clear of perfect might, complete power and comprehensive knowledge, of what He arranged of the causes of guidance and misguidance, of wretchedness and felicity, of salvation and destruction, and it is bound to its beginning, meaning a linkage. The beginning and the end encompass the explanation of this, together with what the middle also includes of it, in the greatest encompassing. Glory be to Him whose descent this is, blessed is His name and exalted is His majesty. There is no god but Him, and there is no power or strength except through Allah. My Lord, make it easy, O Generous One.
